blockchain.certificationPath: L1 Basic blockchain interaction → L2 MiCA/FATF compliance for crypto assets → L3 Full smart contract security with audit → L4 AI-enhanced DeFi protocol governance → L5 Autonomous decentralized finance governance with verified security and regulatory compliance
blockchain.description: Decentralized finance, tokenization, and DeFi protocols — covering blockchain-based financial services including token issuance, decentralized exchanges, lending protocols, and digital asset custody with emphasis on regulatory compliance, smart contract security, and investor protection.
blockchain.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III unless used to evaluate the creditworthiness of natural persons (Annex III §5(b)); Art. 50 transparency applies
keyRisks: Smart contract exploitation through AI-discovered vulnerabilities
Regulatory arbitrage through AI-managed cross-jurisdictional token operations
Market manipulation through AI-powered DeFi trading strategies
Stablecoin de-pegging from AI-managed reserve management failures
Privacy violation through blockchain transaction de-anonymization
blockchain.name: Blockchain & DeFi

questions.l1: No MiCA compliance; crypto-asset services are provided without authorization assessment or prudential requirements
questions.l3: Agent tracks MiCA authorization requirements and maintains compliance documentation, but does not automate ongoing prudential requirement monitoring or client asset segregation verification
questions.l5: Full MiCA CASP compliance with authorization requirement tracking, prudential requirement monitoring per Art. 67, client asset segregation per Art. 70, complaint handling per Art. 71, conflict of interest management per Art. 72, and outsourcing governance per Art. 73
questions.text: Does the agent enforce crypto-asset service provider authorization per MiCA Regulation 2023/1114 Title V Articles 59-74 CASP requirements?

questions.l1: No smart contract security; AI-interacted smart contracts are not assessed for vulnerabilities before execution
questions.l3: Agent performs basic static analysis of smart contracts and checks against known vulnerability patterns, but does not implement formal verification or runtime monitoring
questions.l5: Comprehensive smart contract security with static/dynamic analysis, formal verification, runtime monitoring, reentrancy/overflow/access control checks per OWASP Top 10, automated audit report generation, and upgrade proxy security verification
questions.text: Does the agent implement smart contract security assessment per OWASP Smart Contract Top 10?

questions.l1: No travel rule compliance; virtual asset transfers do not include required originator/beneficiary information
questions.l3: Agent collects and transmits travel rule data for transfers above threshold, but does not implement counterparty VASP verification or sunrise issue management
questions.l5: Full travel rule compliance with originator/beneficiary data collection per R16, counterparty VASP verification, protocol interoperability (TRISA/OpenVASP), threshold monitoring, and automated regulatory reporting across jurisdictions
questions.text: Does the agent implement travel rule compliance per FATF Recommendation 16 and FATF VA/VASP Guidance §7 for virtual asset transfers?

questions.l1: Tokens are handled with no recorded classification
questions.l3: A classification is recorded, but the facts it rests on are not captured or uncertain cases are not escalated
questions.l5: Every token has a dated MiCA classification with the facts used, uncertain cases are escalated with the legal decision recorded, and classifications are re-run when facts change
questions.text: Does the agent record, for each token it handles, a classification under the MiCA Art. 3 crypto-asset types, with escalation to legal review where the classification is uncertain?

questions.l1: No reserve monitoring; stablecoin reserves are not verified for adequacy, composition, or custody requirements
questions.l3: Agent tracks reserve composition and adequacy ratios, but does not implement real-time reserve verification or stress testing
questions.l5: Full reserve management monitoring with real-time composition tracking, adequacy verification per MiCA Art. 36, custody requirement compliance per Art. 37, reserve investment policy monitoring, stress testing, and transparent reserve attestation
questions.text: Does the agent implement stablecoin reserve management monitoring per MiCA 2023/1114 Title III Articles 36-39?

questions.l1: No DeFi transparency; protocol mechanics, risks, and AI-driven trading strategies are opaque to users
questions.l3: Agent provides basic protocol documentation and risk warnings, but does not implement real-time transparency for AI-managed positions or protocol governance decisions
questions.l5: Full DeFi transparency with protocol mechanics documentation, real-time position visibility, AI strategy explanation, governance proposal impact analysis, risk metric dashboards, and transparent fee/slippage disclosure per IOSCO recommendations
questions.text: Does the agent provide DeFi protocol transparency per IOSCO Policy Recommendations for DeFi?

questions.l1: Agent orders are not checked for insider dealing or manipulation patterns
questions.l3: Orders are screened for some patterns, but inside-information restrictions are not enforced on the agent
questions.l5: Every agent order passes pre-submission checks for restricted-list hits and manipulation patterns, blocked orders are logged with reasons, and checks are tested on each release
questions.text: Are the agent's own crypto-asset orders checked before submission so that it does not trade on inside information (MiCA Art. 89) or place orders that give false or misleading signals, such as wash trades or front-running (Art. 91)?

questions.l1: Agent orders and transactions are not recorded with their decision context
questions.l3: Records are kept for five years, but are not linked to the agent's decision or cannot be extended to seven years
questions.l5: Each order and transaction links to the agent decision and inputs, retention is five years with an authority-extension flag, and a sampled reconstruction is tested each quarter
questions.text: Does the CASP keep records of every service, order and transaction the agent performs, linked to the agent's decision, for five years and up to seven where the competent authority requests (MiCA Art. 68(9))?

questions.l1: No surveillance of orders and transactions the agent arranges or executes
questions.l3: Alerts exist, but escalation and reporting to the authority are manual or untracked
questions.l5: Alerts cover the agent's order flow, each alert has a case record and decision, and suspicious-order reports are submitted without delay with submission evidence retained
questions.text: If the agent professionally arranges or executes crypto-asset transactions, do surveillance arrangements detect possible market abuse in orders and transactions, and are reasonable suspicions reported to the competent authority without delay (MiCA Art. 92(1))?

questions.l1: Travel-rule data is applied only above a threshold for EU transfers, or self-hosted transfers are not assessed
questions.l3: No threshold is applied for EU transfers, but self-hosted ownership assessments are manual or unrecorded
questions.l5: No threshold is applied to EU transfers, each self-hosted transfer over EUR 1 000 has a recorded ownership assessment, and transfer value includes fees and FX at a documented rate
questions.text: For transfers of crypto-assets over EUR 1 000 to a self-hosted address, does the agent assess whether the address is owned or controlled by the originator (Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 Art. 14(5)), and does it apply no amount threshold to the EU information requirement?

questions.l1: Transfers are sent without complete originator and beneficiary information
questions.l3: Outgoing transfers are complete, but missing information on incoming transfers is not detected or handled by a documented procedure
questions.l5: Outgoing transfers are validated before sending, incoming transfers are checked for missing information, and every execute/reject/return/suspend decision is recorded with its reason
questions.regulatoryRef: Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 Art. 14; Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 Art. 16; Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 Art. 17
questions.text: Does every crypto-asset transfer the agent sends carry the originator and beneficiary information required by Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 Art. 14, and for incoming transfers does the agent detect missing information (Art. 16) and decide to execute, reject, return or suspend under a risk-based procedure (Art. 17)?

questions.l1: No CFTC perimeter assessment; products are classified only via SEC/Howey or EU categories
questions.l3: Performs a basic commodity vs security analysis, but does not connect results to product-type implications or maintain audit-ready rationale
questions.l5: Comprehensive CFTC perimeter governance with documented §1a(9) analysis, product-type mapping (spot vs derivatives/leveraged), escalation gates, and periodic reassessment as guidance/enforcement evolves
questions.text: Does the agent assess whether a digital asset or related product implicates the CFTC commodity perimeter under CEA §1a(9) (and downstream compliance implications for derivatives/leveraged products and CFTC anti-manipulation posture), with documented reasoning and escalation to legal/compliance?

questions.l1: No suitability assessment before advice or portfolio management
questions.l3: A questionnaire exists, but recommendations are not blocked when it is missing or stale
questions.l5: Recommendations are blocked until a current suitability assessment is recorded, and assessments are retained with the recommendations they supported
questions.text: Before the agent gives advice on crypto-assets or manages a crypto-asset portfolio, does it assess suitability from the client's knowledge and experience, investment objectives including risk tolerance, and financial situation, and record the assessment (MiCA Art. 81(1))?

questions.l1: Tokens are offered to US persons with no recorded securities-status analysis
questions.l3: An analysis is recorded, but distribution and marketing facts are not captured or indicators are not escalated
questions.l5: Every token offered to US persons has a dated Howey analysis with the facts used, indicator hits are escalated with the legal decision recorded, and the analysis is re-run when facts change
questions.regulatoryRef: SEC v. W.J. Howey Co., 328 U.S. 293 (1946)
questions.text: For tokens offered to or traded with US persons, does the agent record a securities-status analysis under the Howey test, including distribution and marketing facts, with escalation to legal review where investment-contract indicators are present?

questions.l1: Non-EU transfers apply no threshold logic, or transfer value is computed inconsistently
questions.l3: A threshold is applied, but fees, FX or split and merged transfers are not included in the valuation
questions.l5: The threshold rule for each non-EU jurisdiction is configured and versioned, transfer value includes fees and FX at a documented rate, split transfers are aggregated, and each decision is retained per transfer
questions.text: For crypto-asset transfers on corridors outside the EU, does the agent apply the travel-rule threshold of FATF Recommendation 15 and its interpretive note, valuing each transfer deterministically including fees, FX and split transfers?

regulatoryReferences.citation: FATF Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and VASPs (2021)
SEC Framework for 'Investment Contract' Analysis of Digital Assets (2019)
ISO/TC 307 Blockchain and distributed ledger technologies standards
BIS CPMI guidance on stablecoin arrangements
IOSCO Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets

circular-economy.certificationPath: L1 Basic ESG data collection → L2 EU Taxonomy alignment assessment → L3 Full sustainable finance compliance with greenwashing prevention → L4 AI-enhanced circular economy investment optimization → L5 Autonomous sustainable finance governance with verified impact outcomes
circular-economy.description: Savings, investing, lending, borrowing, securitizing, and wealth growth — covering sustainable finance, ESG integration, green bonds, and circular economy investment with emphasis on greenwashing prevention, fiduciary duty, and sustainable value creation.
circular-economy.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III; high-risk only under Art. 6(1) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a product covered by Annex I legislation — otherwise Art. 4 (AI literacy), Art. 5 (prohibited practices) and Art. 50 (transparency) apply
keyRisks: Greenwashing through AI-generated sustainability claims without verification
Stranded asset risk from inadequate climate transition assessment
ESG rating manipulation through selective data disclosure
Fiduciary duty breach from ESG integration without financial materiality
Circular economy investment fraud through inflated recycling metrics
circular-economy.name: Circular Economy Finance

questions.l1: No Taxonomy alignment; investment decisions do not assess economic activities against EU Taxonomy technical screening criteria
questions.l3: Agent evaluates activities against Taxonomy TSC for climate mitigation/adaptation, but does not implement full DNSH assessment or minimum social safeguards verification
questions.l5: Full Taxonomy alignment with TSC assessment across all six environmental objectives, DNSH verification per Art. 17, minimum social safeguards per Art. 18, Taxonomy-eligible vs. aligned distinction, and KPI calculation per delegated acts
questions.text: Does the agent assess EU Taxonomy alignment per Regulation 2020/852 Article 3 substantial contribution criteria and Article 17 DNSH principle?

questions.l1: No greenwashing prevention; sustainability claims in investment products are not verified against actual portfolio characteristics
questions.l3: Agent validates basic sustainability claims against portfolio data, but does not implement full SFDR disclosure requirements or detect subtle greenwashing patterns
questions.l5: Comprehensive greenwashing prevention with SFDR Art. 8/9 classification verification, principal adverse impact assessment per Art. 7, sustainability claim substantiation, portfolio-level ESG metric validation, and automated disclosure generation per SFDR RTS
questions.text: Does the agent prevent greenwashing per EU SFDR 2019/2088 Article 6-11 sustainability disclosure requirements?

questions.l1: No physical or transition risk assessment of exposures
questions.l3: Risks are assessed for some portfolios, but scenarios and methods are undocumented
questions.l5: All in-scope exposures are assessed with documented scenarios and methods, results are versioned, and reruns reproduce reported figures
questions.text: Does the agent's climate and environmental risk assessment for the institution's exposures identify and measure physical and transition risks using documented scenarios, as expected by EBA Guidelines on the management of ESG risks (EBA/GL/2025/01)?

questions.l1: No safeguards check; investments are reported as Taxonomy-aligned without verifying minimum social safeguards
questions.l3: Investments are screened against basic social criteria and exclusion lists, but the Art. 18 safeguards are not verified for each investee
questions.l5: Alignment is withheld until each investee's Art. 18 minimum safeguards check (OECD MNE Guidelines, UNGPs, ILO Declaration) is recorded with the evidence used and its date
questions.text: Before an investment is reported as Taxonomy-aligned, does the agent verify the minimum social safeguards of EU Taxonomy Regulation Article 18?

questions.l1: No ESG data quality management; sustainability data is collected without standardized methodology or quality controls
questions.l3: Agent collects ESG data per GRI and performs basic quality checks, but does not validate data against primary sources or assess materiality
questions.l5: Full ESG data governance with GRI reporting principle compliance, double materiality assessment, data quality scoring, primary source validation, and automated ESG report generation with assurance readiness
questions.text: Does the agent manage ESG data quality per GRI Standards 2021 reporting principles?

questions.l1: Scoring models are not inventoried or validated, or governance still cites SR 11-7 only
questions.l3: Scoring models are validated under SR 26-2, but the agentic or generative components have no documented governance
questions.l5: Scoring models have SR 26-2 validation and monitoring records, and agentic components have documented scope limits, logging and human approval points, each reviewed on change
questions.text: Are the non-generative ESG scoring models the agent uses inventoried, validated and monitored under the 2026 interagency model-risk guidance (SR 26-2), and, because that guidance excludes generative and agentic AI, are the agent's generative or agentic components covered by separately documented governance and controls?

questions.l1: No green bond tracking; proceeds allocation and impact reporting for green bonds are not systematically managed
questions.l3: Agent tracks green bond proceeds allocation against eligible project categories, but does not implement full impact reporting or external review management
questions.l5: Comprehensive green bond management with proceeds allocation tracking, impact reporting, EU GBS Taxonomy alignment verification, external review coordination, annual allocation/impact report generation, and post-issuance compliance monitoring
questions.text: Does the agent maintain green bond compliance per EU Green Bond Standard Regulation 2023/2631?

questions.l1: No circularity assessment; investments are not evaluated for circular economy alignment or material efficiency
questions.l3: Agent calculates basic circularity metrics for portfolio companies, but does not implement circular business model assessment
questions.l5: Full circularity assessment with Material Circularity Indicator calculation, circular business model evaluation, waste reduction impact measurement, resource efficiency tracking, and circular economy investment opportunity identification
questions.regulatoryRef: Ellen MacArthur Foundation Material Circularity Indicator
questions.text: Does the agent support circular economy investment assessment per Ellen MacArthur Foundation circularity indicators?

questions.l1: ESRS outputs cannot be traced to a materiality assessment or source data
questions.l3: Data points trace to source data, but not to a recorded materiality decision, or value-chain estimates lack documented methods
questions.l5: Every reported data point links to its materiality decision, source data and estimation method, and a sampled set is reproduced before publication
questions.text: For an undertaking within the amended CSRD scope, can every ESRS data point the agent produces be traced to the double-materiality assessment record and to its source data, including value-chain (Scope 3) estimates?

questions.l1: Emissions figures cannot be reproduced from documented boundaries and methods
questions.l3: Boundaries and methods are documented, but figures cannot be reproduced from logged inputs or change history is missing
questions.l5: Figures are reproduced from logged inputs with documented boundaries, methods and change history, and the assurance provider's sample reproduces without exception
questions.text: For a reporting entity under California Health and Safety Code §38532, does the agent compute scope 1 and scope 2 emissions in conformance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol with documented boundaries and methods, in a form a limited-assurance provider can reproduce?

questions.l1: No Art. 8 KPI disclosures: taxonomy KPIs are not computed or cannot be reconciled to financial statements and activity evidence
questions.l3: Computes taxonomy KPIs for some activities, but mappings, reconciliations, and evidence are incomplete
questions.l5: Full Art. 8 KPI disclosure readiness with traceable mappings, reconciliation to financial statements, evidence links, and repeatable disclosure-generation workflows
questions.text: Does the agent compute and disclose EU Taxonomy Article 8 KPIs (taxonomy-eligible vs taxonomy-aligned turnover, CapEx, OpEx) with traceable mappings from financial line items to underlying economic activities, including evidence for eligibility/alignment and reconciliation to financial statements?

questions.l1: No LCA governance: LCAs are ad-hoc with unclear scope and boundaries and no critical review readiness for external claims
questions.l3: Maintains basic LCA templates and assumptions, but allocation and boundary discipline and critical review readiness are inconsistent
questions.l5: Full ISO 14040 and 14044 governance with goal and scope controls, data quality rules, critical review workflow triggers, and auditable evidence bundles for claim substantiation
questions.text: Does the agent ensure lifecycle assessment (LCA) governance aligned to ISO 14040 and 14044, including (1) explicit goal and scope definition and functional unit, (2) boundary, allocation, and cut-off rules, (3) data quality requirements, and (4) critical review triggers and evidence retention when LCA supports external claims?

questions.l1: The agent sends information requests without checking the size of the recipient
questions.l3: Recipient size is checked, but requests beyond the cap are sent without telling the recipient it may decline
questions.l5: Requests to protected undertakings are limited to the cap by default, any extra request states that it is extra and may be declined, and the self-declaration of size is retained
questions.text: When the agent requests sustainability information from value-chain undertakings with not more than 1 000 employees, does it limit requests to the value-chain cap and tell the undertaking which extra information is requested and that it may decline?

questions.l1: Fund names with ESG-type terms are proposed without checking for an 80% investment policy
questions.l3: The 80% policy is checked when a name is proposed, but quarterly portfolio reviews and departures are not tracked
questions.l5: A name with ESG-type terms is blocked unless an 80% policy is recorded; quarterly reviews and every departure, with its return to compliance within 90 consecutive days, are recorded
questions.text: When the agent proposes or reviews the name of a US registered fund that uses terms such as ESG or sustainable, does it check that the fund has adopted the 80% investment policy that 17 CFR 270.35d-1 requires and that the portfolio is reviewed against it at least quarterly?

questions.l1: Transition-related investment decisions take no account of effects on workers or communities
questions.l3: Effects on workers are noted for some decisions, but are not assessed against the ILO guidelines or recorded
questions.l5: Each transition-related decision records its assessment of effects on workers and communities against the ILO guidelines, and the assessment is reviewed when the decision is revisited
questions.text: Does the agent assess the effects of transition-related investment decisions on workers and communities against the ILO Guidelines for a just transition (2015)?

regulatoryReferences.citation: ISO 14044:2006 Life cycle assessment — Requirements and guidelines (with amendments 2017, 2020)
Ellen MacArthur Foundation circular economy principles

sdgAlignment: SDG 8 — Decent Work and Economic Growth

citizen-services.certificationPath: L1 Basic online service delivery → L2 Accessible, GDPR-compliant services → L3 EU Single Digital Gateway compliance → L4 Full eIDAS 2.0 + EU AI Act compliance → L5 Autonomous citizen-centric AI services with verified equity, accessibility, and democratic accountability
citizen-services.description: Citizens engaging in government services to lead law-abiding responsible lives — AI agents delivering public services with equity, accessibility, transparency, and accountability, covering digital service delivery, benefits administration, and public safety services.
citizen-services.euAIActClassification: Annex III §5(a) — public authorities evaluating eligibility for essential public assistance benefits and services
keyRisks: Systemic service denial for vulnerable populations through AI gatekeeping
Benefits fraud enabled by AI-exploitable verification gaps
Algorithmic discrimination in eligibility determinations
Privacy violations from AI-enabled government data aggregation
Loss of non-digital access channels for elderly/disabled citizens
citizen-services.name: Citizen Services

questions.l1: No accessibility compliance; citizen service AI is inaccessible to persons with disabilities, lacks WCAG 2.1 AA conformance, and provides no alternative access channels
questions.l3: Agent implements WCAG 2.1 AA for primary service interfaces, but does not apply accessibility to all channels or maintain accessibility statements per Art. 7
questions.l5: Full accessibility with WCAG 2.1 AA+ implementation, EU Accessibility Directive Art. 4 compliance, multi-channel service delivery (web, mobile, telephone, in-person), accessibility feedback mechanism, annual accessibility statement per Art. 7, and ATAG 2.0 authoring tool compliance
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Accessibility Directive 2016/2102 Art. 4; WCAG 2.1 AA
questions.text: Does the agent implement universal service accessibility per EU Web Accessibility Directive 2016/2102 Article 4 and WCAG 2.1 AA success criteria for all citizen-facing service channels?

questions.l1: No EU SDG compliance; digital service delivery does not meet Art. 6 quality criteria including completeness, accuracy, and cross-border accessibility
questions.l3: Agent implements core EU SDG Art. 6 quality requirements, but does not maintain Art. 12 user experience statistics or cross-border service integration
questions.l5: Full EU SDG compliance with Art. 6 quality criteria for all procedures, cross-border service delivery per Art. 5, Art. 12 user feedback system, quality statistics reporting to European Commission, and Your Europe portal integration
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Single Digital Gateway Regulation 2018/1724 Article 6 quality criteria for online procedures and Article 12 user feedback requirements?

questions.l1: No non-discrimination controls; AI eligibility assessments may discriminate based on protected characteristics without detection or monitoring
questions.l3: Agent performs periodic bias audits for service AI and implements basic fairness constraints, but does not maintain EU AI Act Art. 10 data governance requirements or continuous discrimination monitoring
questions.l5: Full non-discrimination governance with EU AI Act Art. 10 training data requirements, continuous disparate impact monitoring per ECHR Art. 14, automated adverse outcome investigation, non-discrimination impact assessment for new service AI, and transparent fairness reporting
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 10, 14; ECHR Art. 14
questions.text: Does the agent implement non-discrimination per EU AI Act high-risk requirements for AI systems used in essential government services including benefits administration?

questions.l1: No human oversight or citizen transparency; AI-influenced government service decisions are made without citizen notification or accessible human review mechanism
questions.l3: Agent implements human review capability for flagged AI decisions, but does not provide Art. 13 citizen transparency or systematic human oversight per Art. 14 requirements
questions.l5: Full EU AI Act compliance with Art. 13 citizen notification of AI involvement, Art. 14 human oversight with meaningful review capability, citizen explanation of AI-influenced decisions, contestability mechanisms, and national competent authority system registration
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU AI Act Article 14 human oversight for high-risk AI in essential public services and Article 13 transparency for citizens receiving AI-influenced decisions?

questions.l1: No proportionate data use; citizen service AI accesses and retains all available government data without necessity assessment or purpose limitation controls
questions.l3: Agent implements purpose limitation for primary service functions and restricts cross-purpose data use, but does not conduct systematic proportionality assessments or automated data minimization
questions.l5: Full proportionate data governance with GDPR Art. 6(1)(e) necessity assessment for each service AI, Art. 5(1)(b) purpose limitation technical controls, cross-agency data sharing proportionality gates, citizen data transparency dashboards, and automated retention enforcement
questions.text: Does the agent implement proportionate data use per GDPR Article 6(1)(e) public task processing limitation and Article 5(1)(b) purpose limitation for citizen service AI systems?

questions.l1: No service quality framework; citizen service AI is deployed without user research, usability testing, or systematic quality measurement
questions.l3: Agent implements user feedback collection and basic usability assessment, but does not apply ISO 9241-210 human-centered design process or UN E-Government Survey quality standards
questions.l5: Full human-centered design with ISO 9241-210 iterative design process, user research with representative citizen panels, UN E-Government satisfaction measurement, continuous service improvement cycle, and accessible service design for diverse citizen needs
questions.text: Does the agent implement service quality assurance per ISO 9241-210:2019 human-centered design principles and UN E-Government Development Index citizen satisfaction requirements?

questions.l1: No government cybersecurity framework; citizen-facing AI services are deployed without NIST CSF government profile implementation or FedRAMP-equivalent authorization
questions.l3: Agent implements NIST CSF core functions for service security and has completed basic security assessment, but does not maintain FedRAMP-equivalent continuous monitoring or government community profile alignment
questions.l5: Full government cybersecurity with NIST CSF 2.0 Government Community Profile implementation, FedRAMP Rev. 5 equivalent authorization and continuous monitoring, penetration testing, supply chain risk management for service AI components, and incident response integrated with CISA coordination
questions.regulatoryRef: NIST CSF 2.0 Government Community Profile; FedRAMP Rev. 5
questions.text: Does the agent implement cybersecurity for government digital services per NIST CSF 2.0 Government Profile and FedRAMP Rev. 5 authorization requirements?

questions.l1: No vulnerability assessment; citizen service AI does not identify or proactively support populations at risk of digital exclusion including elderly, disabled, homeless, or undocumented individuals
questions.l3: Agent monitors service utilization patterns and identifies underserved groups, but does not implement proactive outreach or EU AI Act recital-aligned vulnerability protection
questions.l5: Full vulnerability governance with EU AI Act recital-aligned vulnerable population identification, proactive service design for at-risk groups, UN SDG 10 equity monitoring, non-digital alternative channels, outreach to digitally excluded populations, and transparent equity reporting to oversight bodies
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Recitals 47-49; UN SDG 10; UN E-Gov Survey 2024
questions.text: Does the agent implement proactive identification of vulnerable citizen populations per EU AI Act recitals 47-49 and UN SDG 10 Reduced Inequalities to prevent service exclusion?

questions.l1: No fundamental rights impact assessment or AI liability compliance; high-risk citizen service AI lacks Art. 27 FRIA and citizens have no structured redress mechanism for AI-caused service failures
questions.l3: Agent conducts basic impact assessment for citizen service AI, but does not implement EU AI Act Art. 27 fundamental rights impact assessment methodology or prepare for AI Liability Directive redress obligations
questions.l5: Full EU AI Act Art. 27 fundamental rights impact assessment for all high-risk citizen service AI, AI Liability Directive readiness with disclosure obligations, citizen redress mechanisms, causal chain documentation for AI-influenced service decisions, and national competent authority FRIA reporting
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 27; AI Liability Directive Proposal
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU AI Act Article 27 fundamental rights impact assessment for high-risk AI in public services and European Commission AI Liability Directive proposal provisions for citizen redress in AI-caused service failures?

questions.l1: Procedure is not fully online: one or more mandatory steps require in-person/phone/mail workarounds or manual staff intervention, with no exception governance or evidence
questions.l3: Most steps are online, but identity/evidence/payment/decision delivery or redress steps still require offline actions or are inconsistently available across procedures
questions.l5: All SDG procedures are end-to-end fully online with exception governance, evidence of completion rates, cross-border accessibility checks, and auditable proof that offline steps are not mandatory except where legally justified
questions.text: For all SDG-scoped procedures, does the agent ensure the full procedure is available fully online end-to-end (including identification/authentication, guidance, form completion, evidence submission, e-signature where applicable, fee/payment, status tracking, decision delivery, and appeal/redress initiation), with documented exceptions and accessibility-preserving alternative channels, per SDG Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 Article 2(2)?

questions.l1: No cross-border support: identity/credential flows work only for domestic users and fail for cross-border credentials or foreign-issued attributes
questions.l3: Some cross-border scenarios work, but coverage is incomplete, usability is poor, and there is limited evidence of interoperability testing and relying-party validation
questions.l5: Full cross-border readiness with interoperable identity/credential acceptance, relying-party verification, consistent UX across Member States, and audit-ready evidence of cross-border transactions and conformance testing
questions.text: Does the agent support eIDAS 2.0 cross-border use (per §6) by enabling (1) cross-border identification/authentication acceptance, (2) EUDI Wallet or equivalent credential presentation flows where applicable, (3) relying-party verification and attribute validation, (4) multilingual/cross-border error handling and support, and (5) evidence exports demonstrating successful cross-border transactions and interoperability testing?

questions.l1: No focus-order control: keyboard navigation order is illogical, dynamic steps trap focus, or assistive technology users cannot complete procedures
questions.l3: Some pages meet focus order, but complex journeys (wizards/modals/dynamic forms) have inconsistent focus management and limited test evidence
questions.l5: End-to-end focus-order compliance across all journeys with automated checks, AT-supported manual test evidence, and change-control gates preventing regressions
questions.text: Across all citizen-service user journeys (including AI-assisted decision notices, identity steps, uploads, and payments), does the agent ensure WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order is met (logical tab order, focus visibility where relevant, no focus traps, consistent focus management on dynamic updates), with automated regression tests and manual AT test evidence?

questions.l1: No 508 mapping: accessibility is asserted but not evidenced against Revised 508 Standards, with gaps in forms/keyboard/AT compatibility
questions.l3: Partial mapping: some criteria are met and tested, but gaps remain and evidence is not consistently retained or auditable
questions.l5: Full Revised 508 Standards compliance with traceable criteria mapping, repeatable testing, remediation SLAs, and audit-ready evidence bundles
questions.regulatoryRef: Section 508 Revised Standards (36 CFR Part 1194 Appendices A and C)
questions.text: For web-based citizen services, does the agent meet Section 508 Revised Standards (36 CFR Part 1194 Appendices A and C) requirements (including text alternatives, keyboard access, non-interference with assistive tech, form label/field associations, timing control, and accessible documentation), and produce evidence bundles (test reports, exception logs, remediation tracking) suitable for procurement/audit?

questions.l1: Citizens must upload evidence that authorities already hold
questions.l3: Some evidence types are retrieved through the once-only system, but preview and explicit request are not enforced
questions.l5: All available evidence types retrieved through the once-only technical system on explicit request, with preview before use, and logged exchanges
questions.text: For procedures in scope of the Single Digital Gateway Regulation (EU) 2018/1724, does the agent support the Article 14 once-only technical system, retrieving evidence directly from competent authorities at the user's explicit request and letting the user preview it before use?

questions.l1: Applicants are not told that AI is involved in eligibility decisions
questions.l3: A general statement exists on the website, not in the applicant's own case
questions.l5: Notice given in each case before the decision, stating the system's purpose and the right to an explanation, with the notice recorded on the case file
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III §5(a); EU AI Act Art. 26(11)
questions.text: Where the agent supports decisions on eligibility for public assistance benefits and services (EU AI Act Annex III point 5(a)), does the authority inform each applicant that a high-risk AI system is being used, as Article 26(11) requires?

clinical-lifecycle.certificationPath: L1 Basic clinical workflow support → L2 Evidence-based protocol compliance → L3 Full QMS per ISO 13485 with clinical governance → L4 AI-assisted clinical decision-making with FDA/MDR compliance → L5 Autonomous clinical lifecycle governance with verified patient outcomes
clinical-lifecycle.description: Therapeutic, surgical, psychoanalysis, and alternative medicine — covering clinical practice modalities with emphasis on evidence-based practice, patient safety, clinical governance, and treatment efficacy monitoring.
clinical-lifecycle.euAIActClassification: Art. 6(1) and Annex I (Regulation (EU) 2017/745 MDR, 2017/746 IVDR) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a medical device; Annex III §5(d) for emergency healthcare patient triage
keyRisks: Surgical planning errors from AI-generated anatomical analysis
Therapeutic protocol deviation undetected by automated monitoring
Alternative medicine interactions with conventional treatments missed by AI
Clinical governance failure from over-reliance on AI recommendations
Patient harm from AI-managed treatment titration without adequate safety margins
clinical-lifecycle.name: Clinical Lifecycle

questions.l1: No design controls; clinical AI systems are developed without systematic design input/output verification or validation
questions.l3: Agent tracks design control documentation and maintains design and development files per ISO 13485:2016 Clause 7.3, but does not automate design review processes or validation protocol execution
questions.l5: Full design control automation with systematic design input capture, output verification, design review facilitation, validation protocol management, design transfer documentation, and post-market design change control per ISO 13485:2016 Clause 7.3 as required by 21 CFR §820.10
questions.text: Does the agent implement quality management system requirements per the FDA Quality Management System Regulation (21 CFR §820.10, incorporating ISO 13485:2016 by reference from 2 February 2026) and ISO 13485:2016 Clause 7.3 design and development for clinical AI systems?

questions.l1: No guideline adherence monitoring; clinical practices are not systematically compared against current evidence-based guidelines
questions.l3: Agent references major clinical guidelines and flags deviations for common conditions, but does not track guideline currency or manage the full spectrum of applicable guidelines
questions.l5: Comprehensive guideline adherence with real-time protocol compliance monitoring, automated guideline currency tracking, deviation documentation with clinical justification, GRADE evidence quality integration, and outcome-based guideline effectiveness assessment
questions.regulatoryRef: NICE TA Process Guide; WHO Guideline Development Handbook 2nd ed.
questions.text: Does the agent enforce clinical practice guideline adherence per NICE Technology Appraisal process and WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2nd ed.)?

questions.l1: No surgical safety automation; surgical checklists are paper-based with no automated verification or compliance tracking
questions.l3: Agent digitizes the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist with sign-in/time-out/sign-out phases, but does not integrate with surgical scheduling, equipment verification, or post-operative monitoring
questions.l5: Full surgical safety orchestration with automated checklist compliance, surgical scheduling integration, equipment/implant verification, intraoperative monitoring alerts, post-operative complication detection, and surgical outcome tracking per WHO checklist and JCI COP.7
questions.regulatoryRef: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist 2nd ed.; JCI COP.7
questions.text: Does the agent implement surgical safety per WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (2nd ed.) and JCI Standard COP.7 with pre/intra/post-operative verification?

questions.l1: No adverse event automation; clinical adverse events are reported manually with potential underreporting and delayed submissions
questions.l3: Agent facilitates adverse event capture and generates MedWatch/vigilance reports, but does not implement automated event detection or trend analysis
questions.l5: Autonomous adverse event management with automated detection from clinical data, severity classification, MedWatch/EUDAMED report generation, trend analysis for signal detection, root cause analysis facilitation, and CAPA tracking per §803 and MDR Art. 87
questions.text: Does the agent manage adverse event reporting per FDA MedWatch 21 CFR §803 and EU MDR 2017/745 Article 87 vigilance requirements?

questions.l1: No subgroup efficacy analysis; treatment outcomes are not stratified by patient demographics or clinical characteristics
questions.l3: Agent tracks basic outcome metrics by treatment modality, but does not perform subgroup analysis or assess treatment effect heterogeneity
questions.l5: Comprehensive efficacy assessment with estimand-based outcome analysis per ICH E9(R1), subgroup stratification, treatment effect heterogeneity detection, therapeutic equity monitoring, and automated reporting of disparate outcomes for clinical review
questions.regulatoryRef: ICH E9(R1) — Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis
questions.text: Does the agent assess treatment efficacy across patient subgroups per ICH E9(R1) estimands framework and prevent therapeutic inequity?

questions.l1: No clinical audit trail; treatment decisions and modifications are not systematically recorded with attribution
questions.l3: Agent logs major clinical decisions with timestamps and user attribution, but does not implement Part 11 compliant electronic signatures or prevent audit trail tampering
questions.l5: Full Part 11 compliant audit trail with electronic signatures, tamper-evident logging, complete decision provenance including AI recommendation context, physician override documentation, and automated audit trail integrity verification
questions.regulatoryRef: EU MDR 2017/745 Annex I §23.4; FDA 21 CFR Part 11
questions.text: Does the agent maintain clinical audit trail per EU MDR 2017/745 Annex I §23.4 and FDA 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements?

questions.l1: No software lifecycle management; clinical AI updates are deployed without systematic development process controls
questions.l3: Agent tracks software versions and maintains basic change documentation, but does not implement full IEC 62304 software development lifecycle with safety classification-appropriate rigor
questions.l5: Full IEC 62304 compliance with safety classification-driven development rigor, software requirements traceability, architecture documentation, unit/integration/system testing per Clause 5.5-5.7, and maintenance process per Clause 6 with anomaly resolution tracking
questions.text: Does the agent manage medical device software lifecycle per IEC 62304:2006/AMD1:2015 Clause 5 software development process for clinical AI?

questions.l1: No clinical risk management; AI-assisted clinical decisions are not subject to systematic hazard identification or risk assessment
questions.l3: Agent maintains a risk management file with identified hazards for major clinical AI functions, but risk estimation and control measures are not systematically updated with real-world evidence
questions.l5: Comprehensive clinical risk management with systematic hazard identification per Clause 5, quantitative risk estimation per Clause 6, risk control implementation and verification per Clause 7, residual risk evaluation, and continuous post-market risk monitoring with evidence-based updates
questions.text: Does the agent implement clinical risk management per ISO 14971:2019 Clause 5-7 hazard identification, risk estimation, and risk control for AI-assisted clinical decisions?

questions.l1: No shared decision-making support; treatment options are presented without patient preference integration or decision aid tools
questions.l3: Agent presents treatment options with basic risk/benefit information, but does not implement structured decision aids or patient preference elicitation
questions.l5: Full shared decision-making with validated decision aids, patient preference elicitation tools, risk communication per Ottawa DSF, treatment option comparison with personalized outcome predictions, and decision quality measurement
questions.regulatoryRef: NICE Shared Decision Making Guidelines; Ottawa DSF
questions.text: Does the agent support shared clinical decision-making per NICE Shared Decision Making guidelines and Ottawa Decision Support Framework?

questions.l1: No CAM safety integration; alternative medicine use is not tracked or assessed for interactions with conventional treatments
questions.l3: Agent records patient-reported CAM use and checks major herb-drug interaction databases, but does not integrate CAM safety into the overall clinical risk assessment
questions.l5: Comprehensive CAM safety integration with herb-drug interaction checking, evidence quality assessment for CAM interventions per WHO strategy, patient disclosure facilitation, integrative care plan coordination, and adverse event monitoring for CAM-related harms
questions.text: Does the agent implement complementary/alternative medicine safety per WHO Traditional Medicine Strategy 2014-2023 and herb-drug interaction databases?

questions.l1: No PMCF or IVDR compliance; AI clinical workflow agents lack post-market clinical follow-up per MDR Art. 83 and AI-integrated IVD agents are not evaluated per IVDR Annex XIV performance requirements
questions.l3: Agent collects post-market safety data and reports adverse events, but does not implement systematic PMCF per MDR Art. 83 or IVDR Annex XIV performance evaluation for AI-driven IVD workflows
questions.l5: Full MDR Art. 83 PMCF implementation with proactive clinical data collection, IVDR Annex XIV performance evaluation for AI-integrated IVD agents, PMCF plan documentation, periodic safety update reports, and notified body PMCF audit readiness
questions.regulatoryRef: EU MDR Art. 83; IVDR 2017/746 Annex XIV
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU MDR 2017/745 Article 83 post-market clinical follow-up (PMCF) obligations and IVDR 2017/746 Annex XIV performance evaluation for AI-integrated clinical workflow and IVD agents?

questions.l1: No design verification; outputs are not verified against inputs and evidence is missing or ad hoc
questions.l3: Maintains some verification tests and trace links, but coverage is incomplete and acceptance criteria are inconsistently documented
questions.l5: Full design verification governance with protocol templates, defined acceptance criteria, traceability completeness checks, automated gap reporting, and release gating on verification evidence
questions.text: Does the agent manage and evidence design and development verification per FDA 21 CFR §820.10 (QMSR) and ISO 13485:2016 Clause 7.3, including verification planning, objective evidence that design outputs meet design inputs, acceptance criteria, and bidirectional traceability (input → output → verification results)?

questions.l1: No usability evaluation; UI/workflow changes ship without summative evidence for safety-critical tasks
questions.l3: Performs some usability testing, but it is not tied to use-related risk controls and evidence is incomplete for regulated review
questions.l5: Full usability evaluation lifecycle with use-related risk scenarios, representative-user studies, traceability to risk controls, documented residual risk acceptance, and audit-ready reports
questions.text: Does the agent support usability engineering per IEC 62366-1:2015 §5.7 by planning and capturing summative usability evaluation evidence for safety-critical clinical workflows (including use-related risk scenarios, representative users, and documented residual use-related risk)?

questions.l1: No MDR QMS; controls are scattered and not governed by an audit-ready QMS framework
questions.l3: Has documented procedures for some Art. 10(9) elements, but integration, ownership, and evidence linkage are incomplete
questions.l5: Comprehensive MDR QMS orchestration with integrated procedures, evidence pointers per control, automated audit pack generation, and continuous monitoring of QMS effectiveness
questions.text: Does the agent implement and evidence EU MDR 2017/745 Article 10(9) manufacturer QMS requirements, including integrated procedures for risk management, clinical evaluation, PMS/vigilance, control of nonconforming outputs, CAPA, and change control (with role/accountability assignments)?

questions.l1: No controlled design inputs; requirements are informal and not approved or traceable
questions.l3: Maintains requirements, but completeness/conflict checks and approval/traceability are inconsistent
questions.l5: Full design input control with structured requirements, review/approval workflow, conflict detection, regulatory/safety/usability coverage checks, and bidirectional traceability to verification/validation evidence
questions.text: Does the agent manage design and development inputs per ISO 13485:2016 §7.3.3, ensuring inputs are complete/unambiguous, include regulatory + safety + usability requirements, are reviewed/approved, and are traced through outputs, verification, and validation?

questions.l1: No controlled production processes; releases and configuration changes are manual and not validated or monitored
questions.l3: Uses CI/CD and basic change controls, but environment/configuration drift and release validation evidence are incomplete
questions.l5: Fully controlled production controls with validated pipelines, configuration baselines, segregation of duties, monitored production KPIs, deviation/CAPA linkage, and audit-ready release evidence
questions.text: Does the agent enforce production and process controls per FDA 21 CFR §820.10 (QMSR) and ISO 13485:2016 Clause 7.5.1 for clinical AI systems (controlled build/release processes, configuration/environment controls, process validation where applicable, and production monitoring with deviation handling)?

keyRisks: Participant safety compromise from AI-managed dose escalation
Data integrity failures in AI-processed clinical trial data

Selection bias in AI-driven participant recruitment algorithms
Regulatory rejection due to AI-generated data quality issues
clinical-trials.name: Clinical Trials

questions.l1: No safety monitoring automation; adverse events are reported manually with potential delays in serious adverse event detection
questions.l3: Agent tracks adverse events and generates safety reports per §312.32 timelines, but does not implement risk-based monitoring or predictive safety signal detection
questions.l5: Autonomous safety monitoring with risk-based monitoring per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.11.4, real-time SAE detection and 15-day/7-day reporting per §312.32, safety signal detection, DSMB report generation, and automated safety narrative preparation
questions.text: Does the agent implement participant safety monitoring per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.11.4 risk-based monitoring and FDA 21 CFR §312.32 safety reporting?

questions.l1: No digital consent management; informed consent is paper-based with no AI-specific disclosures or ongoing consent verification
questions.l3: Agent manages electronic informed consent with §50.25 required elements and AI disclosures, but does not support dynamic consent for protocol amendments or multimedia consent delivery
questions.l5: Full eConsent with all §50.25 elements, AI-specific disclosures, multimedia delivery, comprehension verification, dynamic re-consent for amendments, ongoing consent monitoring, and IRB-approved consent form version management per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §2.8
questions.text: Does the agent enforce informed consent per FDA 21 CFR §50.25 required elements and ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §2.8 with AI-specific disclosures?

questions.l1: No CDISC compliance; clinical data is collected in proprietary formats without standardized variable definitions
questions.l3: Agent implements CDASH-aligned case report forms and generates SDTM datasets, but does not automate mapping validation or implement full CDISC compliance checking
questions.l5: Full CDISC implementation with CDASH-compliant eCRF design, automated SDTM mapping with Pinnacle 21 validation, ADaM dataset generation, define.xml creation, and end-to-end data standards compliance from collection through submission
questions.regulatoryRef: CDISC CDASH v2.2; CDISC SDTM v2.0
questions.text: Does the agent maintain clinical data standards per CDISC CDASH v2.2 for data collection and SDTM v2.0 for regulatory submission datasets?

questions.l1: No IRB management automation; ethics committee submissions and approvals are tracked manually
questions.l3: Agent tracks IRB submission status and approval timelines, but does not automate continuing review preparation or protocol deviation reporting
questions.l5: Comprehensive IRB management with automated submission preparation, continuing review documentation, protocol deviation reporting, amendment tracking, annual report generation, and multi-site IRB coordination per 21 CFR Part 56 and EU CTR Art. 4
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA 21 CFR Part 56; EU CTR 536/2014 Art. 4
questions.text: Does the agent manage IRB/Ethics Committee oversight per FDA 21 CFR Part 56 and EU CTR 536/2014 Article 4 ethics committee assessment?

questions.l1: No recruitment equity; participant selection algorithms may exclude underrepresented populations or perpetuate historical trial enrollment biases
questions.l3: Agent monitors demographic enrollment metrics and flags underrepresentation, but does not implement proactive diversity recruitment strategies or assess eligibility criteria for unnecessary exclusions
questions.l5: Comprehensive recruitment equity with diversity enrollment targets per FDA guidance, eligibility criteria bias assessment, community engagement integration, decentralized trial access optimization, demographic monitoring dashboards, and automated diversity action plan reporting

questions.text: Does the agent ensure equitable participant recruitment per FDA Diversity Action Plan guidance and ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.1 trial design and participant selection?

questions.l1: No electronic data integrity controls; clinical trial data lacks audit trails, electronic signatures, or systematic validation
questions.l3: Agent implements audit trails and access controls for eCRF data, but does not enforce Part 11 electronic signatures or implement full data validation per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §4.3
questions.l5: Full data integrity with Part 11 compliant electronic signatures, complete audit trails, automated edit check programming, medical coding validation, SAE reconciliation, data lock procedures, and database audit readiness per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §4.3
questions.regulatoryRef: ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §4.3; FDA 21 CFR Part 11
questions.text: Does the agent implement data integrity per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §4.3 computerised systems and FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic trial records?

questions.l1: No trial registration management; registration and results reporting obligations are tracked manually with risk of non-compliance
questions.l3: Agent tracks registration status and results reporting deadlines, but does not automate registration data updates or results submission preparation
questions.l5: Full registration compliance with automated WHO ICTRP data element population, ClinicalTrials.gov registration and update management, results reporting within 42 CFR Part 11 timelines, and protocol registration verification across multiple registries
questions.regulatoryRef: WHO ICTRP Registration Standards; 42 CFR Part 11
questions.text: Does the agent support trial registration per WHO ICTRP standards and ClinicalTrials.gov 42 CFR Part 11 results reporting requirements?

questions.l1: No CONSORT compliance; trial reports do not follow standardized reporting guidelines
questions.l3: Agent generates trial report templates aligned with CONSORT checklist, but does not automate flow diagram generation or validate completeness of every checklist item
questions.l5: Full CONSORT compliance with automated participant flow diagram generation, complete checklist item documentation, subgroup analysis reporting, harm reporting per CONSORT extension, and publication-ready manuscript preparation with all required elements
questions.text: Does the agent support CONSORT 2025 compliant trial reporting with complete and transparent results disclosure?

questions.l1: No supply chain management; investigational product distribution, storage, and accountability are tracked manually
questions.l3: Agent tracks IP inventory and distribution, but does not implement temperature monitoring, expiry management, or randomization-integrated dispensing
questions.l5: Comprehensive IP supply chain with temperature-monitored distribution, expiry management, randomization-integrated dispensing, accountability reconciliation, return/destruction documentation, and blinding integrity verification per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.15.3

questions.text: Does the agent manage clinical trial supply chain per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.15.3 supplying and handling investigational products and EU CTR 536/2014 Article 61?

questions.l1: No vulnerable population protections; consent processes do not differentiate for children, cognitively impaired, or other vulnerable groups
questions.l3: Agent identifies vulnerable participants and applies additional consent requirements, but does not implement age-appropriate assent processes or legally authorized representative management
questions.l5: Full vulnerable population protection with pediatric assent per Subpart D, LAR consent management, cognitively impaired participant safeguards, prisoner protections per Subpart C, pregnancy registry integration, and ongoing capacity assessment per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §2.8
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA 21 CFR Part 50 Subpart D; ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §2.8
questions.text: Does the agent implement vulnerable population protections per FDA 21 CFR Part 50 Subpart D (children) and ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §2.8 special consent provisions?

questions.l1: No E6(R3) compliance; AI clinical trial agents still operate under E6(R2) framework without implementing E6(R3) risk-based quality management, proportionate monitoring, or decentralized trial provisions
questions.l3: Agent implements E6(R2) GCP requirements and basic risk-based monitoring, but does not address E6(R3) proportionate approach to quality management or decentralized trial-specific AI agent requirements

questions.regulatoryRef: ICH E6(R3) Principles and Annex 1 §3.10; EU CTR 536/2014
questions.text: Does the agent implement ICH E6(R3) (Step 4, 6 January 2025) risk-based quality management framework for AI agents in decentralized clinical trials superseding E6(R2) requirements?

questions.l3: Implements basic remote monitoring access and findings tracking, but activity logging, SDV approach documentation, and closure evidence are inconsistent
questions.l5: Full electronic monitoring governance with role-based monitor access, immutable activity logs, SDV/SDR plan management, centralized + on-site monitoring evidence consolidation, CAPA linkage, and inspection-ready monitoring reports
questions.text: Does the agent support electronic/remote monitoring per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.11.4 by enforcing controlled monitor access to electronic systems (eSource/EDC/eTMF), logging monitor activities/findings, supporting documented SDV/SDR approaches, and ensuring follow-up actions are tracked to closure?

questions.l1: No EU CTR safety reporting; SUSAR/periodic safety reporting is manual, inconsistent, or not traceable to source safety cases
questions.l3: Tracks EU safety cases and reporting deadlines, but reconciliation, completeness checks, and submission evidence are incomplete
questions.l5: Full EU CTR safety reporting automation with SUSAR + periodic safety report orchestration, case/report reconciliation, submission evidence retention, audit trails, and continuous compliance monitoring across member states
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU CTR 536/2014 Articles 41-43 safety reporting workflows (including SUSAR reporting and periodic/annual safety reporting), with jurisdiction-aware timelines, submission readiness tracking, and reconciliation against case processing to ensure completeness and timeliness?

questions.l1: No retention governance; site records are incomplete or retention periods are not tracked/enforced
questions.l3: Maintains records and basic retention policies, but trigger-based retention scheduling, completeness checks, and retrieval readiness are inconsistent
questions.l5: Full §312.62 compliance with record completeness checks, trigger-based retention automation, defensible destruction holds, rapid retrieval/export for inspection, and cross-system linkage (EDC/eSource/pharmacy/IRB) with audit logs
questions.text: Does the agent enforce investigator recordkeeping and retention per FDA 21 CFR §312.62, including complete case histories, drug disposition records, and retention scheduling based on regulatory triggers (e.g., 2 years after marketing application approval or discontinuation/withdrawal notice)?

questions.l1: No Helsinki governance; approvals are not reliably tracked and study activities can proceed without confirmed independent ethics approval
questions.l3: Tracks ethics approvals, but enforcement (no-start gating) and condition/continuing oversight tracking are inconsistent
questions.l5: Full Helsinki-aligned ethics governance with no-start/no-change gates, approval condition tracking, continuing oversight reminders, deviation/escalation workflows, and audit-ready ethics committee evidence exports
questions.text: Does the agent implement research ethics committee governance consistent with Declaration of Helsinki §23 by ensuring protocol/materials are submitted for independent ethics review and approval prior to trial start, tracking conditions/approvals, and preventing study activities prior to documented approval?

questions.l1: No GDPR research basis/safeguards; health data is processed without a documented Art. 9(2)(j) basis or consistent safeguards
questions.l3: Documents a research basis and applies some safeguards (e.g., pseudonyms), but minimization, retention, and access governance are inconsistent across systems/vendors
questions.l5: Full GDPR research governance with documented lawful basis, safeguards-by-default across EDC/eSource/analytics, automated retention + access reviews, DPIA linkage, and audit-ready evidence for supervisory authorities and partners
questions.text: Does the agent implement GDPR special-category health data processing for scientific research under Art. 9(2)(j), including Art. 89 safeguards (pseudonymisation where possible, purpose limitation, data minimization, access controls, and retention governance) for clinical trial datasets and operational systems?

cognition-to-intelligence.certificationPath: L1 Basic data processing → L2 GDPR-compliant profiling controls → L3 EU AI Act high-risk compliance → L4 ISO 42001 AI management certified → L5 Autonomous explainable intelligence with continuous bias monitoring and democratic oversight
cognition-to-intelligence.description: Contextual data interpretation moving from master data through meta, empirical, analytical, to contextual intelligence — profiled, personalized, and preferentiated — AI agents that transform raw data into actionable, trusted intelligence with explainability and bias controls.
cognition-to-intelligence.euAIActClassification: Chapter V obligations for general-purpose AI models (Art. 53; Art. 51 classification with systemic risk) where the agent provides or integrates a GPAI model; Art. 50 transparency for systems interacting with natural persons
keyRisks: Discriminatory automated decisions affecting rights per GDPR Art. 22
Context collapse in personalization leading to filter bubbles
Opaque intelligence surfaces eroding human agency
Data quality degradation amplified by AI inference chains
Over-personalization enabling manipulation and behavioral nudging
cognition-to-intelligence.name: Cognition to Intelligence

questions.l1: No explainability; AI intelligence outputs are black-box with no explanation of reasoning, confidence, or input data usage
questions.l3: Agent provides post-hoc explanations for key outputs using LIME/SHAP-style attribution, but does not implement IEEE 7001 transparency process documentation

questions.text: Does the agent prevent discriminatory automated decisions per GDPR Article 22 and EU AI Act Article 10 data governance for training data bias?

questions.l1: No AI management system; intelligence AI operates without systematic risk assessment, monitoring, or improvement processes

questions.l5: Full ISO 42001 AIMS implementation with Annex A controls, continuous AI risk assessment and treatment, AI system performance monitoring, stakeholder impact assessment, and systematic improvement cycle documentation
questions.text: Does the agent implement AI system lifecycle management per ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Annex A controls including risk assessment and continuous improvement?

questions.l1: No AI risk mapping; deployed intelligence systems lack systematic contextualization of risks and impacts

questions.l5: Full NIST AI RMF MAP function implementation with continuous risk categorization, impact assessment across stakeholder categories, risk tolerance documentation, and integration with MEASURE and MANAGE functions
questions.text: Does the agent implement NIST AI RMF Map function requirements for contextual risk identification in deployed intelligence systems?

questions.l1: No data minimization in AI pipelines; personal data is retained indefinitely in training data, model weights, and inference caches without purpose review

questions.l3: Agent implements basic human oversight checkpoints and respects user privacy preferences, but does not systematically assess UNESCO ethics principle alignment

questions.text: Does the agent implement adversarial robustness per NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.6 and OWASP ML Security Top 10 for model extraction and inference attacks?

questions.l1: No cryptographic identity security; digital identity verification relies on low-assurance credentials without phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication or hardware-bound key management
questions.l3: Agent implements MFA for identity services and uses PKI certificates, but does not meet ISO/IEC 29115 LoA4 requirements or NIST SP 800-63B AAL3 hardware-bound authenticator requirements
questions.l5: Full cryptographic identity security with ISO/IEC 29115 LoA4 compliance, NIST SP 800-63B AAL3 phishing-resistant authenticators, hardware security module integration, biometric binding with liveness detection, and cryptographic audit trail for all identity assertions
questions.text: Does the agent implement cryptographic security for digital identity per ISO/IEC 29115:2013 entity authentication assurance level 4 requirements and NIST SP 800-63B authenticator assurance level 3?

questions.l1: No identity breach response; identity system incidents are handled without GDPR Art. 33 notification timelines or NIS2 significant incident escalation procedures
questions.l3: Agent detects identity system anomalies and can initiate breach notification, but does not automate GDPR Art. 33 72-hour notification or NIS2 Art. 23 competent authority reporting
questions.l5: Full identity incident response with automated GDPR Art. 33 notification within 72 hours, NIS2 Art. 23 significant incident reporting, affected identity holder notification per Art. 34, credential revocation workflows, and forensic-ready audit evidence preservation
questions.text: Does the agent implement breach notification and identity compromise response per GDPR Article 33 72-hour notification and EU NIS2 Directive Article 23 for identity infrastructure incidents?

questions.l1: No social scoring prohibition or remedy compliance; government identity AI may implement social scoring without Art. 5(1)(d) assessment and citizens lack CoE Convention Art. 14 remedy for AI-influenced identity decisions
questions.l3: Agent restricts scoring-based identity decisions and provides basic appeal mechanisms, but does not implement Art. 5(1)(d) social scoring prohibition assessment or CoE Convention Art. 14 procedural safeguards
questions.l5: Full EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(d) social scoring prohibition with automated detection, CoE AI Convention Art. 14 remedy and procedural safeguards, citizen notification of AI-influenced decisions, effective contestability mechanisms, and transparent governance reporting to national human rights institutions
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(d); CoE AI Convention Art. 14
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU AI Act Article 5(1)(d) prohibition on AI social scoring by public authorities and Council of Europe AI Convention 2024 Article 14 remedy and procedural safeguards for citizens affected by AI identity decisions?

questions.l1: No Art. 5a wallet control: wallet assurance level high is not defined, evidenced, or auditably enforced
questions.l3: Some wallet features exist (e.g., selective disclosure), but assurance level high governance and evidence are incomplete or non-auditable
questions.l5: Full Art. 5a EUDI Wallet implementation with assurance level high governance, relying-party verification, cross-border acceptance, and auditor-ready evidence packs for issuance/authentication/attestation lifecycles
questions.regulatoryRef: eIDAS 2.0 Art. 5a (EUDI Wallet); assurance level high
questions.text: Does the agent implement eIDAS 2.0 Article 5a EU Digital Identity Wallet requirements with explicit support for wallet assurance level high, including (1) assurance claim governance, (2) evidence bundles for high assurance (issuance + authentication + attribute attestation), (3) relying-party verification flows, (4) cross-border acceptance checks, and (5) auditable wallet lifecycle controls (issuance, suspension, revocation, recovery)?

questions.l1: No Annex III lifecycle: identity AI lacks risk management, data governance, logging, and FRIA evidence
questions.l3: Some controls exist (e.g., transparency, incident response), but lifecycle evidence and conformity-assessment readiness are incomplete
questions.l5: Full Annex III §8 lifecycle operationalization with conformity-assessment-grade evidence packs, FRIA workflow, and ongoing monitoring/reporting
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III §8 (high-risk) — lifecycle obligations
questions.text: For EU AI Act Annex III §8 high-risk use cases in digital identity and citizen-rights systems, does the agent implement the full high-risk lifecycle (risk management system, dataset governance, event logging, technical documentation, post-market monitoring, incident reporting, and a fundamental-rights impact assessment workflow for public-sector deployments), with evidence exports suitable for oversight inquiries?

questions.l1: No explicit-consent controls: special-category attributes are processed/shared without explicit consent evidence or withdrawal handling
questions.l3: Consent is captured, but is not granular/purpose-scoped or lacks auditable receipts and withdrawal enforcement
questions.l5: Full Art. 9(2)(a) explicit-consent governance with granular consent receipts, withdrawal enforcement, and audit-ready logs tied to attribute disclosure events
questions.text: When special-category attributes are stored or shared via the digital identity wallet, does the agent implement GDPR Art. 9(2)(a) explicit consent with (1) purpose-scoped consent prompts, (2) granular attribute-level consent, (3) withdrawal/refresh rules, (4) consent receipt + audit logs, and (5) safeguards against coerced consent in public-service contexts?

questions.l1: No AL3 mapping: assurance controls are inconsistent and cannot be evidenced against §7 AL3
questions.l3: Some strong auth controls exist, but AL3 mapping and audit evidence are incomplete
questions.l5: Full §7 AL3 operationalization with clear control mapping, consistent enforcement, and auditor-ready evidence packs
questions.text: Does the agent implement ISO/IEC 29115:2013 §7 assurance level AL3 for entity authentication (and map wallet flows to AL3), including identity proofing strength, authenticator requirements, binding/recovery, phishing resistance expectations appropriate to AL3, and evidence for auditors that AL3 controls are consistently applied across services?

questions.l1: No mapping governance: citations drift and requested anchors (e.g., Art. 5a) are not consistently used
questions.l3: Mapping exists but updates are manual and inconsistently applied
questions.l5: Versioned, reviewed control mapping with automated citation-consistency checks and audit-defensible references
questions.text: Does the program maintain a versioned eIDAS 2.0 control-to-article mapping for the EUDI Wallet (ensuring Art. 5a anchors are used where required), with review on regulatory updates and automated checks for citation consistency across questions and outputs?

questions.l1: Affected persons cannot obtain any explanation of the AI system's role
questions.l3: Explanations are given on request, but they are generic and not specific to the decision
questions.l5: Decision-specific explanations generated from logged inputs and outputs, delivered in plain language within a set time, and tracked through to any appeal
questions.text: When a decision based on the output of an Annex III high-risk AI system produces legal effects for a person, can the affected person obtain a clear and meaningful explanation of the AI system's role and the main elements of the decision, as EU AI Act Article 86 provides?
