digital-health-record.certificationPath: L1 Basic EHR data capture → L2 HL7 FHIR interoperability → L3 Full HIPAA/GDPR compliant data governance → L4 Cross-border health data exchange per EHDS → L5 Autonomous longitudinal health record governance with patient-sovereign data control
digital-health-record.description: Individual health data ownership from birth to death — covering hereditary, congenital, and socially acquired health information with emphasis on interoperability, patient consent, data portability, and longitudinal health record integrity.
digital-health-record.euAIActClassification: Art. 6(1) and Annex I (Regulation (EU) 2017/745 MDR, 2017/746 IVDR) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a medical device; Annex III §5(a) where public authorities use it to evaluate eligibility for healthcare services
keyRisks: PHI breach through AI-mediated data aggregation across systems
Health record integrity compromise from automated data reconciliation errors
Genetic discrimination from AI-accessible hereditary health data
Patient consent violation through automated data sharing without granular authorization
Interoperability failures causing clinical decision errors from incomplete records
digital-health-record.name: Digital Health Record

questions.l1: No HIPAA-compliant authentication; EHR access lacks unique user identification and multi-factor authentication
questions.l3: Agent enforces unique user IDs and role-based access per §164.312(a)(1), with MFA for remote access, but does not implement context-aware authentication or behavioral anomaly detection
questions.l5: Zero-trust EHR access with continuous authentication, behavioral biometrics, context-aware access decisions, break-glass emergency protocols with post-hoc audit, and cryptographic proof of every access event per §164.312(d)
questions.text: Does the agent enforce HIPAA §164.312(a)(1) unique user identification and §164.312(d) person/entity authentication for all EHR access?

questions.l1: No information blocking awareness; data sharing requests are handled inconsistently with potential blocking behaviors
questions.l3: Agent identifies and prevents common information blocking practices per 45 CFR §171 exceptions framework, but does not proactively facilitate data access or track blocking complaints
questions.l5: Full information blocking prevention with proactive data availability, automated exception documentation per §171.201-§171.204, patient access facilitation, third-party app integration support, and transparent blocking incident reporting
questions.text: Does the agent implement information blocking prevention per 21st Century Cures Act §4004 and ONC Final Rule 45 CFR Part 171?

questions.l1: No provenance tracking; health record modifications are not systematically attributed or timestamped
questions.l3: Agent creates FHIR Provenance resources for major record events (creation, updates) but does not capture granular field-level changes or cross-system provenance chains
questions.l5: Comprehensive provenance with field-level change tracking, cross-system provenance chains using FHIR Provenance.agent and Provenance.entity, W3C PROV-DM alignment, immutable audit trail, and provenance verification for clinical decision support inputs
questions.text: Does the agent maintain HL7 FHIR R4 Provenance resources per FHIR specification §6.1.1 for all health record modifications?

questions.l1: No digital consent management; patient consent is paper-based with no granular data sharing controls
questions.l3: Agent manages FHIR Consent resources with basic permit/deny policies, but does not support granular purpose-of-use consent or dynamic consent modification by patients
questions.l5: Patient-sovereign consent management with granular purpose-of-use controls, dynamic consent modification, consent propagation across federated systems, automated consent enforcement at data access point, and transparent consent audit trail per GDPR Art. 7(1)
questions.regulatoryRef: HL7 FHIR R4 Consent Resource; GDPR Art. 9(2)(a)
questions.text: Does the agent support patient consent management per FHIR Consent resource and GDPR Article 9(2)(a) explicit consent for health data processing?

questions.l1: No encryption enforcement; PHI may be stored or transmitted without encryption
questions.l3: Agent enforces AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit for PHI, but does not manage encryption key lifecycle or implement end-to-end encryption for patient-facing data
questions.l5: Full PHI encryption with AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, end-to-end encryption for patient portals, hardware security module key management, automated key rotation, and encryption verification in audit logs per §164.312(a)(2)(iv)
questions.text: Does the agent implement encryption per HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(iv) encryption at rest and §164.312(e)(1) transmission security for all PHI?

questions.l1: No cross-border data exchange capability; health records are siloed within national systems
questions.l3: Agent supports basic cross-border data exchange using EU eHealth Network patient summary format, but does not implement full EHDS secondary use provisions or data permit management
questions.l5: Full EHDS compliance with primary use data exchange via MyHealth@EU, secondary use data permit management per Chapter IV, data quality assessment, pseudonymization, and cross-border interoperability testing certification
questions.regulatoryRef: EU EHDS Regulation Ch. II (Art. 23 MyHealth@EU); Ch. IV
questions.text: Does the agent support cross-border health data exchange per EU EHDS Regulation Chapter II primary use (Art. 23 MyHealth@EU) and Chapter IV secondary use provisions?

questions.l1: No genetic data protections; hereditary health information is accessible without additional safeguards beyond general PHI controls
questions.l3: Agent classifies genetic data separately and applies enhanced access controls, but does not prevent indirect genetic inference from non-genetic health data or manage genetic counseling consent
questions.l5: Comprehensive genetic data governance with enhanced classification, inference prevention controls, genetic counseling consent tracking, research use consent management per GINA §102, and automated genetic discrimination risk assessment for data sharing requests
questions.text: Does the agent prevent genetic discrimination per Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act (GINA) Title I §101 and GDPR Article 9(1) genetic data protections?

questions.l1: No ISO 27799 alignment; health information security controls are ad hoc without systematic implementation
questions.l3: Agent implements ISO 27799 access control and cryptographic controls, but does not maintain the full control set or perform regular security assessments per Clause 7.2
questions.l5: Full ISO 27799 implementation with all Clause 7 controls, regular security assessment automation, health-specific threat modeling, incident management per Clause 7.2.6, and continuous compliance monitoring with evidence collection
questions.text: Does the agent maintain ISO 27799:2025 health information security controls including access control policy and cryptographic controls?

questions.l1: No IHE profile implementation; document sharing is proprietary with no standardized metadata
questions.l3: Agent implements XDS.b document registration and query with proper metadata per ITI TF-3, but cross-community access via XCA is not supported
questions.l5: Full IHE integration with XDS.b document lifecycle management, XCA cross-community queries, XCPD patient discovery, metadata quality validation, and automated document relationship management per ITI TF-3 §4.2
questions.regulatoryRef: IHE ITI TF-3 §4.2 — XDS.b; IHE XCA Profile
questions.text: Does the agent support IHE XDS.b document sharing with metadata per IHE ITI TF-3 §4.2 and cross-community access per XCA profile?

questions.l1: No data quality assessment; health record completeness and accuracy are not systematically measured
questions.l3: Agent performs basic completeness checks against USCDI data classes and flags missing required elements, but does not assess data accuracy, timeliness, or consistency across sources
questions.l5: Comprehensive data quality management with completeness scoring against USCDI v4 data classes, accuracy validation through cross-source reconciliation, timeliness monitoring, consistency checks, and automated data quality improvement recommendations
questions.regulatoryRef: HL7 FHIR Data Quality Framework; USCDI v4
questions.text: Does the agent implement data quality assessment per HL7 FHIR Data Quality Framework and USCDI v4 data class completeness requirements?

questions.l1: No minimum necessary enforcement; users can access full patient records regardless of their role or purpose
questions.l3: Agent implements role-based access that limits PHI exposure by job function, but does not dynamically adjust access based on specific transaction purpose or clinical context
questions.l5: Dynamic minimum necessary enforcement with purpose-of-use based access filtering, clinical context awareness, automated de-identification for non-treatment uses per §164.514(a), and granular field-level access logging
questions.text: Does the agent enforce minimum necessary standard per HIPAA §164.502(b) and §164.514(d) for all PHI disclosures and internal access?

questions.l1: No EU AI Act registration or ONC HTI-1 compliance; EHR AI systems are not registered in the EU high-risk AI database and bulk FHIR export operations lack auditable-event logging
questions.l3: Agent maintains EU AI Act technical documentation and supports FHIR bulk export, but does not automate Art. 49 registration or §170.315(d)(2) auditable-event logging for bulk data access
questions.l5: Full EU AI Act Art. 49 registration with technical documentation, §170.315(d)(2) auditable-event logging for (g)(10) bulk FHIR export, 21st Century Cures Act §4004 information-blocking prevention for AI-mediated record access, and conformity assessment documentation
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU AI Act Article 49 registration for Annex III high-risk systems and audit logging for bulk FHIR access through the ONC standardized API criterion (45 CFR §170.315(g)(10)) with auditable events per §170.315(d)(2)?

questions.l1: No controls to detect/avoid information blocking; restrictions and delays are handled ad hoc with no exception documentation
questions.l3: Tracks common blocking scenarios and can document some exceptions, but monitoring is incomplete and patient/app requests still experience avoidable delays
questions.l5: Continuous information-blocking prevention with automated request intake/SLAs, proactive data availability, exception selection + evidence bundle generation, complaint-ready reporting, and governance review of any access/exchange/use limitation
questions.text: Does the agent implement and evidence information blocking compliance per 21st Century Cures Act §4004, including operational monitoring for access/exchange/use delays and documented use of applicable exceptions when limiting access?

questions.l1: PHI is transmitted without enforced encryption and without documented risk-based decisions or compensating controls
questions.l3: PHI is generally protected with TLS for major interfaces, but enforcement is inconsistent across integrations and there is no formal documentation of encryption decisions/controls
questions.l5: Enforced encryption for all ePHI transmissions (TLS 1.3+ / mutually authenticated channels where appropriate), continuous configuration validation, documented risk analysis for any exception, compensating controls, and auditable evidence of encryption posture per interface
questions.text: Does the agent implement and enforce PHI transmission encryption per HIPAA §164.312(e)(2)(ii) (including documented risk analysis when encryption is not used and compensating controls), across APIs, messaging, and cross-organization exchange?

questions.l1: Audit logs are incomplete, user-editable, or not time-stamped; record changes cannot be reliably reconstructed
questions.l3: Maintains audit logs and timestamps for key events, but tamper resistance, retention controls, and linkage to record lifecycle events are incomplete
questions.l5: Immutable audit trail (WORM/append-only), cryptographic integrity verification, time synchronization controls, complete record lifecycle capture, retention/archival controls, and regulator-ready exports aligned to Part 11 expectations
questions.text: Does the agent maintain secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails for creation/modification/deletion of regulated electronic records per 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(e), including tamper detection and secure retention?

questions.l1: No clinical evaluation governance; clinical evidence is not tracked and changes do not trigger evaluation updates
questions.l3: Maintains a clinical evaluation plan and some evidence linkage, but updates are manual and post-market data is not systematically incorporated
questions.l5: Continuous clinical evaluation lifecycle with evidence graph linkage to features/claims, change-triggered evaluation updates, post-market surveillance signal ingestion, and audit-ready clinical evaluation reporting per Art. 61
questions.text: If the system (or modules) are MDR-relevant software, does the agent support EU MDR 2017/745 Article 61 clinical evaluation governance (clinical evidence linkage, evaluation plan, update triggers, and post-market data incorporation)?

questions.l1: FHIR endpoints are partial/non-conformant; no published capability statement or conformance testing; integrations are brittle
questions.l3: Publishes capability statement and supports common interactions, but conformance testing is incomplete and edge cases cause interoperability failures
questions.l5: Verified conformance to §3.3 with automated conformance test suites, versioning/compatibility guarantees, published capability statements, and continuous monitoring of exchange failures with remediation workflows
questions.text: Does the agent conform to HL7 FHIR R4 §3.3 interoperability requirements for API behavior and exchange (including required interactions/constraints and conformance assertions), with testable evidence (e.g., capability statements and conformance tests)?

questions.l1: No standards-compliant ITI-18 query; document discovery is proprietary or incomplete
questions.l3: Supports basic ITI-18 queries, but coverage is incomplete (edge cases, error handling, security assertions) and interoperability testing is limited
questions.l5: Full ITI-18 compliance with automated conformance testing, robust error handling, security assertions aligned to deployment, and continuous interoperability regression testing across communities
questions.text: Does the agent implement IHE XDS.b ITI-18 (Registry Stored Query) correctly (query parameters, response structure, error handling, and security), validated via interoperability testing?

digital-payments.certificationPath: L1 Basic payment processing → L2 PCI DSS v4.0.1 compliance → L3 Full PSD2/AML compliance with fraud detection → L4 AI-enhanced cross-border payment optimization → L5 Autonomous payment ecosystem governance with verified security and inclusion
digital-payments.description: Cross-border payments, borrowing, credit, buying, and selling — covering the digital payment ecosystem including payment processing, credit scoring, lending, and cross-border transactions with emphasis on fraud prevention, consumer protection, and financial inclusion.
digital-payments.euAIActClassification: Annex III §5(b) — evaluating the creditworthiness of natural persons or establishing their credit score (financial-fraud detection excluded)
keyRisks: AI-enabled payment fraud at scale through adversarial attacks
Credit scoring discrimination against protected classes
Cross-border AML compliance failures from jurisdictional complexity
Consumer data exploitation through open banking API abuse
Systemic risk from AI-managed high-frequency payment routing
digital-payments.name: Digital Payments

questions.l1: Account data appears in agent prompts, transcripts or logs, or is stored or transmitted in clear text
questions.l3: Stored and transmitted account data are protected, but agent prompts, transcripts and logs are not scanned for PAN
questions.l5: Automated scanning of prompts, transcripts, tool payloads and logs finds no PAN on every release, stored account data is unreadable, transmissions use strong cryptography, and the agent components are inside the entity's PCI DSS assessment scope
questions.regulatoryRef: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 3; PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 4
questions.text: Does the agent keep primary account numbers out of prompts, transcripts, tool payloads and logs, render any account data it stores unreadable, and use strong cryptography whenever it transmits account data over open networks (PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirements 3 and 4)?

questions.l1: No AML/KYC automation; customer identification and due diligence are manual processes with inconsistent application
questions.l3: Agent performs automated CDD with identity verification and sanctions screening, but does not implement enhanced due diligence for high-risk customers or ongoing monitoring
questions.l5: Comprehensive AML/KYC with risk-based CDD per FATF R10, automated CIP per §1020.220, enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk jurisdictions, ongoing transaction monitoring, suspicious activity detection, and automated SAR filing preparation
questions.text: Does the agent enforce AML/KYC per FATF Recommendation 10 (Customer Due Diligence) and FinCEN BSA 31 CFR §1020.220 CIP requirements?

questions.l1: Prohibited-basis attributes or known proxies can enter the scoring model and no test exists
questions.l3: Prohibited-basis attributes are excluded from inputs, but proxy testing is not performed for every model version
questions.l5: Inputs exclude prohibited bases, every model version has a recorded proxy test with results and remediation, and the records are retained with the model version
questions.text: Does the agent's credit-scoring logic exclude prohibited bases and features that act as proxies for them, with a recorded proxy test for every model version (12 CFR 1002.6(b); 15 U.S.C. 1691(a))?

questions.l1: Agent-initiated payments complete without strong customer authentication
questions.l3: Strong customer authentication is applied, but the authentication code is not bound to amount and payee or the agent can change them after authentication
questions.l5: Every agent-initiated payment is authenticated with an amount- and payee-specific code shown to the payer, any post-authentication change invalidates the code, and tests cover web and app channels
questions.regulatoryRef: PSD2 2015/2366 Art. 97; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389 Art. 4; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389 Art. 5
questions.text: For electronic payments the agent initiates, does the flow apply strong customer authentication (PSD2 Art. 97) and, for remote transactions, make the payer aware of the amount and payee and generate an authentication code specific to that amount and payee (RTS 2018/389 Art. 5)?

questions.l1: No fee transparency; payment fees, exchange rates, and total costs are not clearly disclosed before transaction execution
questions.l3: Agent displays fees and exchange rates before transaction confirmation, but does not provide comparative cost information or total cost of payment calculations
questions.l5: Full fee transparency with pre-transaction total cost disclosure, comparative fee analysis, exchange rate markup transparency, recurring payment cost projections, and machine-readable fee schedules per PSD2 Art. 45
questions.text: Does the agent provide payment fee transparency per PSD2 Article 45 information on charges?

questions.l1: No real-time fraud detection; payment transactions are not screened for fraud indicators before authorization
questions.l3: Agent performs rule-based fraud screening with basic velocity checks and geolocation verification, but does not implement ML-based behavioral analysis or network-level fraud detection
questions.l5: Advanced fraud detection with ML behavioral analysis, device fingerprinting, network graph analysis, real-time risk scoring per EMV 3DS 2.3, and automated fraud case management
questions.text: Does the agent implement real-time fraud detection per EMV 3-D Secure 2.3 risk-based authentication?

questions.l1: Transfers are sent without complete payer or payee information
questions.l3: Required fields are populated for most transfers, but incomplete transfers are not held or rejected
questions.l5: Every transfer is validated for complete payer and payee information before sending, incomplete transfers are held or rejected under a documented rule, and the evidence is retained per transfer
questions.text: For each transfer of funds the agent initiates or prepares, does the required payer and payee information accompany the transfer (Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 Art. 4), and are transfers with incomplete information held or rejected?

questions.l1: Transaction records lack the agent's decision inputs or are not retained
questions.l3: Transactions are retained for five years, but the agent's decision inputs and model version are not linked to them
questions.l5: Each transaction record links to the agent's inputs, rules or model version and outcome, is retained at least five years, and a sampled dispute is reconstructed from the records each quarter
questions.text: Does the agent retain transaction records, including the inputs, rules or model version behind each fraud or risk decision it made, for at least five years in a form usable for dispute resolution and supervisory examination?

questions.l1: Agent model or API providers are not in the register of information
questions.l3: Providers are in the register, but risk assessment or contract terms are missing for some of them
questions.l5: Every provider the agent calls is in the register with risk assessment, contract terms and exit plan, and the register is reconciled against the agent's live dependency list on each release
questions.text: Is every ICT third-party service the payment agent depends on (model or API providers included) recorded in the DORA register of information and managed under the entity's ICT third-party risk policy?

questions.l1: No payment-page script governance: scripts are loaded without authorization controls or integrity monitoring, allowing silent skimming or exfiltration
questions.l3: Maintains a script inventory and basic CSP, but integrity or change detection and alerting are incomplete and not audit-ready
questions.l5: Full PCI 6.4.3 readiness with authorized-script allowlisting, continuous integrity monitoring (SRI/CSP/hashes), automated change approval workflows, real-time alerting or blocking for unauthorized scripts, and audit evidence bundles for assessor review
questions.text: For payment pages, does the agent enforce PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 6.4.3 by maintaining an authorized script inventory, validating each script legitimacy (source/owner/purpose), implementing change detection and integrity controls (e.g., SRI/CSP/script hashing), and alerting or blocking on unauthorized or modified scripts that could capture payment data?

questions.l1: Agent incidents are not classified or reported on DORA time limits
questions.l3: Incidents are classified, but reporting clocks are tracked manually or some limits were missed without notifying the authority
questions.l5: Classification runs on every agent incident, 4h/24h/72h/one-month timers are enforced, and submissions and any late-submission notices are retained
questions.regulatoryRef: EU DORA Art. 18; EU DORA Art. 19; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301 Art. 5
questions.text: Are ICT incidents involving the agent classified under DORA criteria and, when major, reported within the RTS time limits: initial notification within 4 hours of classification and no later than 24 hours after awareness, intermediate report within 72 hours of the initial notification, final report within one month?

questions.l1: Transfers are authorised without verification of payee
questions.l3: Verification of payee runs, but the agent can proceed after a mismatch without an explicit payer decision
questions.l5: Every transfer records the verification result before authorisation, close-match and no-match force an explicit payer decision, and tests cover match, close-match, no-match and not-possible outcomes
questions.text: For credit transfers in euro that the agent prepares or initiates, is verification of payee obtained before the payer authorises, is any close match or mismatch shown to the payer, and does the agent refuse to authorise on the payer's behalf after a mismatch?

questions.l1: The agent is outside the resilience testing programme
questions.l3: The agent is included in annual vulnerability scans, but scenario-based tests and remediation tracking are missing
questions.l5: Risk-based test plan covering the agent and its dependencies (vulnerability assessments, scenario and performance tests, source code review where relevant), independent testers, and findings tracked to closure
questions.text: Are the agent and the ICT systems it relies on covered by the digital operational resilience testing programme required by DORA (EU) 2022/2554 Articles 24 and 25, including vulnerability assessments, scenario-based tests and tracked remediation of findings?

questions.l1: No fundamental rights impact assessment
questions.l3: An assessment exists, but it is not tied to the deployed version or not updated on change
questions.l5: The assessment is versioned with the deployed system, covers the processes, affected groups, risks, human-oversight and mitigation measures, and is updated on every material change
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 27; EU AI Act Annex III §5(b)
questions.text: Before deploying an AI system that evaluates the creditworthiness or credit score of natural persons, has the deployer completed a fundamental rights impact assessment under AI Act Art. 27(1), tied to the deployed version?

questions.l1: Remittance transfers can be paid for without a pre-payment disclosure
questions.l3: A disclosure is shown, but it omits applicable elements (such as the exchange rate or covered third-party fees) or is shown after payment in some channels
questions.l5: Payment is blocked until a pre-payment disclosure with every applicable §1005.31(b)(1) element is shown, for agent-initiated and user-initiated transfers alike, and the disclosure shown is retained with the transfer
questions.text: For remittance transfers the agent initiates or prepares, is the sender given the pre-payment disclosure of 12 CFR 1005.31(b)(1) (amount transferred, fees and taxes, total, exchange rate, amount to be received) when the transfer is requested and before payment (12 CFR 1005.31(e)(1))?

drug-discovery.certificationPath: L1 Basic research data management → L2 FAIR data compliance with CDISC standards → L3 Full GMP/GLP compliant AI-assisted discovery → L4 ICH Q8-Q12 quality-by-design integration → L5 Autonomous drug discovery governance with verified reproducibility and regulatory submission readiness
drug-discovery.description: Biological research, molecules, drug and therapy production — covering the drug discovery pipeline from target identification through lead optimization, preclinical development, and manufacturing with emphasis on data integrity, reproducibility, and regulatory compliance.
drug-discovery.euAIActClassification: Out of scope under Art. 2(6) when developed and put into service solely for scientific research and development; otherwise Art. 6(1) and Annex I (Regulation (EU) 2017/745 MDR, 2017/746 IVDR) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a medical device
keyRisks: AI-generated molecular candidates with hidden toxicity profiles
Data integrity failures in AI-managed laboratory information systems
Irreproducible AI-discovered drug targets due to training data bias
GMP violations from AI-optimized manufacturing process changes
Intellectual property disputes over AI-generated molecular structures
drug-discovery.name: Drug Discovery

questions.l1: No ALCOA+ enforcement; research data lacks systematic attributability, legibility, contemporaneity, originality, and accuracy controls
questions.l3: Agent enforces basic data integrity controls with audit trails and access management, but does not implement full ALCOA+ across all data lifecycle stages or validate computerized system data integrity
questions.l5: Full ALCOA+ data integrity with automated attribution, contemporaneous recording verification, original data preservation, accuracy validation, completeness checks, consistency monitoring, enduring storage, and availability assurance per GMP Annex 11 §7
questions.text: Does the agent enforce data integrity per FDA 21 CFR §211.68 and EU GMP Annex 11 §7 ALCOA+ principles for all discovery data?

questions.l1: No QbD integration; drug development processes are not designed with systematic quality risk management
questions.l3: Agent supports design space exploration and basic risk assessment per ICH Q9, but does not implement full QbD lifecycle including control strategy development
questions.l5: Comprehensive QbD with target product profile definition, critical quality attribute identification, design space characterization per ICH Q8(R2), quality risk management per ICH Q9, control strategy per ICH Q10, and lifecycle management per ICH Q12
questions.text: Does the agent implement Quality by Design (QbD) per ICH Q8(R2) §2.6 design space and ICH Q9 quality risk management for AI-assisted drug development?

questions.l1: No FAIR compliance; research data is siloed, poorly documented, and not interoperable across systems
questions.l3: Agent assigns persistent identifiers and basic metadata to datasets, but interoperability and reusability are limited by proprietary formats and incomplete documentation
questions.l5: Full FAIR implementation with persistent identifiers (DOI), rich metadata per CDISC standards, machine-readable data formats, provenance documentation, license specification, community standard compliance, and automated FAIR maturity assessment
questions.regulatoryRef: FAIR Guiding Principles (Wilkinson et al. 2016); CDISC Foundational Standards
questions.text: Does the agent maintain FAIR data principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) per FAIR Guiding Principles and CDISC data standards for research datasets?

questions.l1: No computational toxicology; molecular candidates are not screened for mutagenic or toxic potential using in silico methods
questions.l3: Agent performs basic QSAR toxicity predictions for lead compounds, but does not implement full ICH M7 assessment workflow or validate predictions against experimental data
questions.l5: Comprehensive computational toxicology with multi-model QSAR screening, ICH M7(R2) compliant mutagenicity assessment, ADMET prediction, off-target activity profiling, structural alert identification, and prediction confidence calibration with experimental validation tracking
questions.regulatoryRef: ICH M7(R2); FDA QSAR Guidance for Mutagenic Impurities
questions.text: Does the agent implement computational toxicology screening per ICH M7(R2) assessment of mutagenic impurities and FDA QSAR guidance?

questions.l1: No IP management; AI-assisted discoveries are not systematically documented for patent protection or inventorship determination
questions.l3: Agent logs AI contributions to discovery processes and maintains invention disclosure records, but does not implement systematic inventorship analysis or freedom-to-operate assessment
questions.l5: Full IP governance with automated invention disclosure capture, AI contribution documentation per USPTO guidance, freedom-to-operate analysis, prior art monitoring, patent landscape mapping, and inventorship determination support for AI-assisted discoveries
questions.regulatoryRef: WIPO PCT; USPTO AI Inventorship Guidance (2024)
questions.text: Does the agent manage intellectual property documentation per WIPO Patent Cooperation Treaty and inventorship determination for AI-assisted discoveries?

questions.l1: No GMP automation; manufacturing procedures and batch records are managed manually without AI-assisted process optimization controls
questions.l3: Agent generates batch production records and tracks process parameters, but AI-recommended process changes are not validated through formal change control per §211.100
questions.l5: Full GMP compliance with automated batch record generation per §211.188, AI process optimization within validated design space, formal change control for AI-recommended modifications, deviation management, and CAPA tracking per §211.192
questions.text: Does the agent enforce GMP manufacturing controls per FDA 21 CFR §211.100 written procedures and §211.188 batch production records for AI-optimized processes?

questions.l1: No CTD preparation support; quality documentation for regulatory submissions is compiled manually
questions.l3: Agent assists with CTD Module 3 document compilation and cross-references, but does not automate data extraction from laboratory systems or validate completeness against ICH requirements
questions.l5: Autonomous CTD Module 3 preparation with automated data extraction from LIMS/ELN, document compilation per ICH M4 structure, cross-reference validation, completeness checking, and submission-ready package generation with eCTD formatting
questions.text: Does the agent support regulatory submission preparation per ICH M4 Common Technical Document (CTD) Module 3 quality documentation?

questions.l1: No responsible AI practices; drug discovery AI may perpetuate biases in target selection or compound optimization
questions.l3: Agent documents AI model training data and performs basic bias checks, but does not implement systematic fairness assessment or diverse population representation in molecular modeling
questions.l5: Comprehensive responsible AI with training data diversity assessment, algorithmic bias testing across therapeutic areas, model interpretability documentation, diverse population pharmacogenomic consideration, and transparent AI methodology reporting per OECD principles
questions.text: Does the agent implement responsible AI practices for drug discovery per OECD AI Principles and prevent algorithmic bias in target identification and lead optimization?

questions.l1: No ELN integrity controls; laboratory records lack electronic signature, audit trail, or tamper-evidence requirements
questions.l3: Agent implements basic ELN with audit trails and access controls, but does not enforce Part 11 compliant electronic signatures or implement full Annex 11 §9 audit trail review processes
questions.l5: Full ELN integrity with Part 11 electronic signatures, Annex 11 §9 compliant audit trails, tamper-evident recording, automated audit trail review, data backup per Annex 11 §7.2, and periodic integrity verification
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; EU GMP Annex 11 §9
questions.text: Does the agent maintain electronic laboratory notebook (ELN) integrity per FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11 §9 audit trail requirements?

questions.l1: No GLP compliance; preclinical study data is not managed per good laboratory practice requirements
questions.l3: Agent tracks study protocols and raw data per GLP requirements, but does not automate study director oversight, QA auditing, or archive management
questions.l5: Full GLP compliance with automated study protocol management, raw data integrity assurance, QA audit scheduling and tracking, specimen/sample accountability, archive management per §58.190, and study report generation per §58.185
questions.regulatoryRef: OECD GLP Principles §8; FDA 21 CFR Part 58
questions.text: Does the agent implement preclinical study data management per OECD GLP Principles §8 and FDA 21 CFR Part 58 good laboratory practice?

questions.l1: No Q9(R1) or Annex 11 §11 compliance; AI quality risk management does not implement updated Q9(R1) 2023 formality-of-risk-management guidance and AI batch release agents lack §11 validation
questions.l3: Agent implements basic quality risk management and validates batch release processes, but does not distinguish ICH Q9(R1) 2023 updates from prior Q9 or implement EU GMP Annex 11 §11 specific batch release AI validation
questions.l5: Full ICH Q9(R1) 2023 compliance with Annex II AI-assisted risk management, formality-of-risk-management calibration, EU GMP Annex 11 §11 batch release AI validation, computerized system validation documentation, and continuous risk review per Q9(R1) lifecycle approach
questions.regulatoryRef: ICH Q9(R1) 2023 Annex II; EU GMP Annex 11 §11
questions.text: Does the agent implement ICH Q9(R1) 2023 revision Annex II AI-assisted quality risk management and EU GMP Annex 11 §11 batch release AI agent validation requirements?

questions.l1: No PQS; quality governance is ad-hoc, roles are unclear, CAPA or change management are inconsistent or absent
questions.l3: Partial PQS with documented roles and some CAPA or change control, but monitoring, management review, and lifecycle governance of AI-driven changes are incomplete
questions.l5: Full ICH Q10 §3.2 PQS with governance, KPIs, CAPA effectiveness checks, formal change management (including AI model or process changes), management review cadence, and audit-ready evidence linkage across discovery, development, and manufacturing
questions.text: Does the agent implement a Pharmaceutical Quality System (PQS) aligned to ICH Q10 §3.2, including defined management responsibilities, process performance or product quality monitoring, CAPA, change management, and management review for AI-assisted discovery and AI-influenced CMC or manufacturing activities?

questions.l1: No post-approval change governance; ECs or PACMP are not defined and AI-driven changes are uncontrolled
questions.l3: Tracks changes and drafts regulatory justifications, but ECs or PACMP scope and reporting categories are inconsistently applied and not audit-ready
questions.l5: Full Q12 §3.2 lifecycle management with EC identification, PACMP workflows, change categorization by region, impact assessment tied to QRM, and submission or notification-ready evidence bundles
questions.text: Does the agent support ICH Q12 §3.2 post-approval change management by defining and controlling Established Conditions (ECs), managing PACMP or predefined change protocols, and maintaining a lifecycle management plan for AI-driven process or model changes that affect CQAs or CPPs?

questions.l1: No §7.1 controls; critical data can be entered or edited without effective verification or falsification controls
questions.l3: Implements some access controls and audit trails, but critical data verification, raw-data linkage, and falsification detection are inconsistent
questions.l5: Comprehensive §7.1 controls with enforced workflows for critical data entry, verification rules, raw-data provenance linkage, anomaly detection, periodic review, and inspection-ready evidence outputs
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU GMP Annex 11 §7.1 data integrity controls for critical data capture (e.g., controlled data entry, verification or second-person review where required, prevention or detection of falsification, and linkage of raw data to reported results) across ELN, LIMS, or instrument integrations?

questions.l1: No CSV or controls; lab computerized systems are unvalidated and rely on informal checks
questions.l3: Validates key systems and performs some checks or backups, but validation scope, change control, and periodic review are incomplete or inconsistently evidenced
questions.l5: Full §211.68-aligned CSV with risk-based validation, documented checks, controlled configuration, backup or restore verification, and continuous monitoring with audit-ready validation packages
questions.text: Does the agent ensure computerized systems used in discovery or CMC labs are validated and controlled per FDA 21 CFR §211.68 (including documented validation, input or output checks, access controls, change control, backup or restore testing, and periodic review) for ELN, LIMS, or instrument integrations?

questions.l1: No design space; operating ranges and boundaries are informal and not supported by evidence
questions.l3: Defines operating ranges and explores multivariate effects, but boundaries, evidence linkage, and within or outside design-space change rules are not consistently enforced
questions.l5: Full §2.2 design space governance with evidence-backed boundaries, linkage to CQAs or CPPs, within or outside design-space change workflows, and alignment to Q9 QRM and Q10 control strategy
questions.text: Does the agent define, justify, and govern a design space per ICH Q8(R2) §2.2 (including explicit boundaries, supporting evidence, and change handling within vs outside design space) for AI-assisted development and AI-influenced process optimization?

regulatoryReferences.citation: FDA Current Good Manufacturing Practice for Finished Pharmaceuticals (21 CFR Parts 210 and 211)
ISO 17511:2020 In vitro diagnostic medical devices — metrological traceability
FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data

farm-to-fork.certificationPath: L1 Basic food safety awareness → L2 HACCP-aligned digital controls → L3 ISO 22000 certified traceability → L4 Full supply chain transparency with EUDR compliance → L5 Autonomous farm-to-fork governance with cryptographic provenance chains
farm-to-fork.description: Sustainable farming, food nutrition, and responsible consumption — covering the entire agri-food value chain from primary production through processing, distribution, and consumption with emphasis on food safety, traceability, and environmental sustainability.
farm-to-fork.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III; high-risk only under Art. 6(1) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a product covered by Annex I legislation — otherwise Art. 4 (AI literacy), Art. 5 (prohibited practices) and Art. 50 (transparency) apply (Annex III §2 covers critical digital infrastructure, road traffic and water, gas, heating or electricity supply, not food systems)
keyRisks: Food fraud and adulteration in AI-managed supply chains
Pesticide residue misclassification by automated monitoring
Deforestation-linked sourcing undetected by traceability agents
Allergen cross-contamination from automated production scheduling
Loss of smallholder farmer livelihoods through algorithmic procurement bias
farm-to-fork.name: Farm to Fork

questions.l1: No HACCP integration; food safety checks are manual and inconsistent with no digital monitoring of critical control points
questions.l3: Agent monitors critical control points in real-time with automated alerts and logs deviations per HACCP plan, but corrective actions still require human initiation
questions.l5: Fully autonomous HACCP orchestration with predictive deviation detection, automated corrective actions, cryptographic evidence chains for each CCP, and continuous validation against Codex standards
questions.text: Does the agent enforce HACCP critical control point monitoring with automated corrective actions per Codex Alimentarius CAC/RCP 1-1969 §7.6?

questions.l1: No digital traceability; paper-based records with gaps in supply chain visibility beyond immediate supplier
questions.l3: Batch-level traceability across major supply chain nodes with digital records, but gaps exist in sub-supplier and smallholder farm-level data
questions.l5: Item-level cryptographic traceability from seed/feed origin through every transformation and logistics step to point of sale, with immutable audit trail and sub-second recall capability
questions.text: Can the agent provide end-to-end supply chain traceability from farm origin to consumer per EU General Food Law Regulation (EC) 178/2002 Article 18?

questions.l1: No deforestation risk assessment; sourcing decisions made without geolocation verification or land-use change analysis
questions.l3: Agent performs periodic geolocation checks against deforestation databases for high-risk commodities, but verification is not continuous and covers only tier-1 suppliers
questions.l5: Continuous satellite-integrated deforestation monitoring for all commodity sourcing tiers, automated due diligence statements per EUDR Art. 4, with predictive land-use change modeling and supplier risk scoring
questions.text: Does the agent verify deforestation-free sourcing compliance per EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) 2023/1115 Article 3?

questions.l1: No organic compliance tracking; certification status managed manually with risk of non-compliant input usage
questions.l3: Agent tracks organic certification status and flags non-compliant inputs, but does not proactively manage the full certification lifecycle or audit readiness
questions.l5: Autonomous organic compliance management including input substance verification against Annex II permitted lists, contamination risk modeling, group certification coordination, and automated audit evidence generation
questions.text: Does the agent manage organic certification compliance per EU Organic Regulation 2018/848 Articles 9-12 including input substance verification?

questions.l1: No automated allergen tracking; allergen declarations managed manually with high cross-contamination risk in production scheduling
questions.l3: Agent maintains allergen databases and validates labeling against Annex II 14 allergen categories, but cross-contamination risk from production sequencing is not algorithmically managed
questions.l5: Full allergen lifecycle management with production line sequencing optimization to minimize cross-contamination, real-time label verification, precautionary allergen labeling risk assessment, and consumer-facing allergen transparency APIs
questions.text: Does the agent implement allergen management controls per EU Food Information Regulation (EU) 1169/2011 Article 21 and Annex II?

questions.l1: No nutritional profiling capability; nutritional data is static and not validated against actual product composition changes
questions.l3: Agent calculates nutritional profiles for products and generates Nutri-Score ratings, but does not dynamically update when formulations or sourcing change
questions.l5: Dynamic nutritional profiling that auto-updates with formulation changes, integrates with reformulation optimization to improve health outcomes, and provides transparent methodology documentation for consumer trust
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Farm to Fork Strategy — Nutritional Labeling Initiative
questions.text: Does the agent support nutritional profiling and front-of-pack labeling accuracy per EU Farm to Fork Strategy Nutri-Score framework?

questions.l1: No fair trade assessment; procurement algorithms optimize purely on cost without considering farmer welfare or equitable pricing
questions.l3: Agent includes fair trade certification status in procurement decisions and tracks minimum price guarantees, but does not assess broader socioeconomic impact on farming communities
questions.l5: Comprehensive farmer welfare integration with living income benchmarking, equitable pricing algorithms, smallholder inclusion metrics, and transparent impact reporting aligned with FAO VGGT principles
questions.text: Does the agent assess fair trade and smallholder farmer impact per FAO Voluntary Guidelines on Responsible Governance of Tenure (VGGT) Principle 3?

questions.l1: No systematic documentation; food safety records are fragmented across systems with no automated evidence collection
questions.l3: Agent generates and stores food safety documentation with structured templates, but evidence collection requires manual triggers and cross-referencing
questions.l5: Fully automated food safety management system with continuous evidence collection, prerequisite program monitoring, audit-ready documentation generation, and real-time compliance dashboards per ISO 22000 Clause 7.5
questions.text: Does the agent maintain food safety management system documentation per ISO 22000:2018 Clause 7.5 with automated evidence collection?

questions.l1: No FSMA compliance; AI food safety agents operate without preventive control plans, hazard analysis, or supply chain program requirements per 21 CFR §117 Subpart C
questions.l3: Agent implements hazard analysis and preventive controls for primary food safety risks, but does not automate supply chain program verification per §117.415 or maintain FSMA §204 traceability records for high-risk foods
questions.l5: Full FSMA compliance with automated hazard analysis per §117.130, preventive control management per §117.135-145, supply chain program verification per §117.415, FSMA §204 Key Data Element traceability for FDA-designated high-risk foods, and corrective action automation per §117.150
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA FSMA 21 CFR §117; FDA FSMA §204 Food Traceability Rule
questions.text: Does the agent implement FDA FSMA 21 CFR §117 Preventive Controls for Human Food requirements for AI agents managing food safety plans in US-market manufacturing facilities?

questions.l1: Cannot reliably identify immediate supplier/customer for lots; records are incomplete or not retrievable on request within operational timeframes
questions.l3: Maintains supplier and customer identities for lots/batches and can produce them on request, but with delays and gaps for intermediaries, rework, and split/merge operations
questions.l5: Real-time, audited one-step-back/one-step-forward traceability with automated lot genealogy (split/merge/rework), instant authority-ready exports, and continuous reconciliation against ERP/WMS events
questions.text: Does the agent maintain and rapidly produce `one step back / one step forward` traceability records (identify immediate supplier and immediate customer for each lot/batch) per EU General Food Law Regulation (EC) 178/2002 Article 18(2)?

questions.l1: No systematic hazard analysis; hazards/control measures are implicit or undocumented and CCP/OPRP choices are not validated
questions.l3: Performs documented hazard analysis and proposes CCP/OPRP assignments with evidence references, but validation is periodic and requires substantial manual review
questions.l5: Continuously maintained hazard analysis with automated evidence ingestion (process changes, incidents, supplier changes), validated CCP/OPRP logic, and on-change revalidation workflows with signed approvals
questions.text: Does the agent support HACCP hazard analysis and validated selection of control measures (including CCP/OPRP determination and validation) per Codex CAC/RCP 1-1969 §3.2?

questions.l1: Control measures are not implemented in workflows; monitoring/correction is ad-hoc and not linked to hazard analysis outputs
questions.l3: Implements control measures and monitors key parameters, but corrections and verification are not consistently linked to ISO 22000 evidence and change control
questions.l5: Closed-loop hazard control with automated monitoring, corrections, verification activities, and change-controlled linkage from hazard analysis to operational parameters and audit evidence
questions.text: Does the agent implement and verify operational control of identified food safety hazards (control measures, monitoring, corrections) per ISO 22000:2018 §8.5.4?

questions.l1: No certification lifecycle tracking; certificate scope/validity is unknown or unmanaged
questions.l3: Tracks certificates and renewal dates and flags expired/invalid scope, but relies on manual updates and does not reconcile against control body records
questions.l5: Automated certificate lifecycle management with control-body reconciliation, scope change workflows, product-claim gating, and audit-ready evidence packs
questions.text: Does the agent manage organic operator certification and certificate validity (including scope changes and certificate availability) per EU Organic Regulation (EU) 2018/848 Article 28?

questions.l1: No worker welfare evidence; labor conditions are unmanaged by the agent
questions.l3: Tracks welfare-related checklists and incidents, but evidence is incomplete and not linked to remediation workflows
questions.l5: Continuous worker welfare assurance with auditable evidence capture, remediation tracking, grievance intake, and KPI reporting aligned to AF.10 controls
questions.text: Does the agent verify and maintain evidence for worker welfare controls on farms per GLOBALG.A.P. IFA v6 AF.10 (worker welfare)?

questions.l1: No due diligence statements are generated or retained; products are placed without required declarations
questions.l3: Generates due diligence statements for some products/suppliers, but coverage is incomplete and supporting evidence is not consistently retained
questions.l5: Automated due diligence statement generation and retention for all relevant products with evidence linkage (geolocation, risk assessment, mitigation) and audit-ready exports
questions.text: Does the agent operate an EUDR due diligence system and generate/retain due diligence statements for relevant products before placing them on the EU market per EUDR 2023/1115 Article 4(2) and Article 5?

questions.l1: No recall workflow; actions are improvised and authority notifications are inconsistent
questions.l3: Has documented recall steps and contact lists with semi-automated batch identification, but execution and notification are manual and slow
questions.l5: Automated recall orchestration with instant affected-lot identification, notification templating, authority-ready evidence bundles, and post-incident CAPA tracking
questions.text: Does the agent support rapid product withdrawal/recall decisioning and competent authority notification workflows per EU General Food Law Regulation (EC) 178/2002 Article 19(1)–(3)?

regulatoryReferences.citation: European Commission, A Farm to Fork Strategy, COM(2020) 381
Codex Alimentarius (incl. General Principles of Food Hygiene CXC 1-1969)
Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 (Deforestation Regulation), as amended by Regulations (EU) 2024/3234 and 2025/2650

freight-3pl-warehouse.certificationPath: L1 Manual freight and warehouse exception review → L2 basic carrier/WMS event capture → L3 SLA, OTIF, inventory, and exception evidence tied to agent decisions → L4 cross-enterprise EPCIS/EDI/API traceability with resilience tests → L5 autonomous logistics reliability governance with signed scorecards, fallback proofs, and continuous KPI drift monitoring
freight-3pl-warehouse.description: Operational logistics agents managing freight tenders, carrier scorecards, 3PL execution, warehouse events, delivery exceptions, cold-chain deviations, and traceability evidence across shippers, carriers, warehouses, and customers.
freight-3pl-warehouse.euAIActClassification: Annex III §4(b) where the agent allocates warehouse or driver tasks based on individual behaviour or personal traits, or monitors and evaluates worker performance; §2 only for safety components in road traffic
keyRisks: Late, missed, damaged, or lost shipments hidden by weak carrier scorecards
Inventory mismatch or pick/pack errors caused by AI-directed warehouse actions
Delivery exceptions routed without ownership, SLA timers, or customer-safe escalation
Cold-chain or chain-of-custody breaks accepted without signed evidence
3PL, EDI, or carrier API outages causing silent fulfillment failure
freight-3pl-warehouse.name: Freight, 3PL & Warehouse Operations

questions.l1: No carrier scorecards; routing decisions ignore observed late, missed, damaged, or lost shipment patterns
questions.l3: Carrier scorecards track core delivery outcomes and inform routing, but evidence is batch-updated and exceptions are reviewed manually
questions.l5: Continuous carrier reliability scoring with signed OTIF/DIFOT evidence, exception-adjusted routing, lane-level drift detection, and auditable decision traces for every carrier recommendation
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO 28000:2022; ISO 9001:2026 (monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation)
questions.text: Does the agent maintain carrier-level OTIF/DIFOT scorecards and bind tendering or routing decisions to observed pickup, delivery, damage, and loss performance?

questions.l1: Exceptions are handled through ad-hoc messages with no owner, SLA timer, or closure evidence
questions.l3: Exceptions are logged with owners and basic SLA timers, but escalation, customer communication, and root-cause evidence are incomplete
questions.l5: Closed-loop exception command center with auto-classification, owner assignment, SLA breach prediction, customer-safe escalation, root-cause tagging, and signed closure evidence
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO 28000:2022 §8; NIST SP 800-161r1-upd1 incident response controls
questions.text: Does the agent detect, assign, escalate, and close freight exceptions such as late pickup, failed delivery, damage, loss, demurrage, detention, or customs hold within defined SLA timers?

questions.l1: Warehouse actions are recommended without inventory reconciliation, pick/pack error checks, or cycle-count evidence
questions.l3: WMS events are checked for major mismatches, but adjustments and pick/pack quality evidence are incomplete
questions.l5: Real-time WMS integrity loop with inventory accuracy monitoring, pick/pack error detection, cycle-count evidence, quarantined adjustments, and rollback-ready fulfillment decisions
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO 9001:2026 (control of production and service provision); GS1 EPCIS 2.0
questions.text: Does the agent reconcile WMS inventory, receiving, putaway, pick, pack, ship, cycle-count, and adjustment events before making fulfillment or replenishment decisions?

questions.l1: Traceability stops at internal order IDs and cannot reconstruct cross-enterprise custody
questions.l3: Shipment and warehouse events include some IDs, but cross-party event sharing and custody gaps remain
questions.l5: EPCIS/GS1-aligned visibility events with SSCC/lot/container references, custody handoff signatures, event completeness checks, and audit-ready route reconstruction
questions.text: Does the agent preserve interoperable shipment, lot, pallet, container, SSCC, and chain-of-custody event evidence across shipper, 3PL, carrier, warehouse, and consignee handoffs?

questions.l1: Condition-sensitive shipments can be released without telemetry, excursion review, or quarantine evidence
questions.l3: Condition telemetry is captured and excursions are flagged, but release blocking and corrective evidence are inconsistent
questions.l5: Continuous condition monitoring with excursion classification, quarantine/release gates, corrective action evidence, customer/regulatory notification workflow, and trend analytics by lane/carrier/facility
questions.text: For temperature-, humidity-, shock-, or seal-sensitive freight, does the agent monitor condition evidence, detect excursions, and block unsafe release until review or corrective action is complete?

questions.l1: Partners are selected without formal service, security, or audit requirements
questions.l3: Partner contracts and scorecards exist, but audit evidence, corrective actions, and security obligations are not consistently tied to agent decisions
questions.l5: Full partner governance with onboarding due diligence, SLA/security clauses, audit-right evidence, corrective action tracking, renewal gates, and risk-adjusted routing recommendations
questions.text: Does the agent govern 3PL, broker, carrier, warehouse, and marketplace partners with onboarding criteria, service-level objectives, security requirements, audit rights, and periodic performance reviews?

questions.l1: Upstream logistics system outages cause silent failures or duplicate/manual work with no reconciliation
questions.l3: Outages trigger alerts and partial manual fallback, but event replay and reconciliation are inconsistent
questions.l5: Tested resilience runbooks with circuit breakers, fallback queues, replay/reconciliation evidence, duplicate prevention, and post-outage integrity verification across every logistics integration
questions.regulatoryRef: EU NIS2 Art. 21; NIST SP 800-161r1-upd1 contingency planning controls
questions.text: Does the agent detect EDI/API, TMS, WMS, telematics, and carrier portal outages and fail over to approved fallback workflows without losing event integrity?

questions.l1: KPIs exist outside AMC and do not affect maturity, routing, or remediation
questions.l3: Some KPIs are reported in dashboards, but they are not consistently bound to evidence or maturity recommendations
questions.l5: KPI-to-AMC mapping is versioned, signed, and continuously monitored with threshold drift alerts, evidence links, and remediation playbooks for every degraded KPI
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO 9001:2026 (monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation); ISO 28000:2022 performance evaluation
questions.text: Does the agent map logistics KPIs such as OTIF/DIFOT, fill rate, inventory accuracy, dock-to-stock time, exception aging, carrier acceptance, and SLA breach rate to AMC maturity evidence?

questions.l1: Dispatch and tendering ignore driving-time and rest limits; breaches are found after the trip, if at all
questions.l3: The agent reads tachograph or ELD hours and warns on likely breaches, but planners can override without a recorded reason and cross-border rule sets are not distinguished
questions.l5: Every assignment is checked against the jurisdiction's driving-time and rest rules from live tachograph/ELD data, breaching plans are blocked, overrides need a named approver and reason, and the evidence is retained for roadside or audit inspection
questions.text: Before proposing or accepting a load plan, does the agent check driver availability against driving-time, break and rest limits — Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 for EU road transport and FMCSA hours-of-service rules at 49 CFR Part 395 in the US — and refuse assignments that would breach them?

questions.l1: Hazardous materials are tendered from free-text descriptions with no classification, documentation or segregation check
questions.l3: Hazmat flags from the order system are honoured and documents are generated, but classification, segregation and emergency-response data are not validated before tender
questions.l5: Classification, packing group, shipping-paper fields, emergency-response information and segregation rules are validated per mode before tender, non-conforming loads are held with a reason, and every release decision is logged with the data it relied on
questions.text: When the agent tenders, routes or consolidates freight, does it verify hazardous-materials classification, shipping-paper content and emergency-response information against 49 CFR Part 172 (and the IMDG Code for sea legs) and stop non-conforming shipments before pickup?

questions.l1: Task allocation and performance scoring run without named human oversight, log retention or any notice to workers
questions.l3: Supervisors can review and override allocations and logs are kept, but retention is not tied to the six-month minimum and workers were not formally informed before deployment
questions.l5: Named, trained overseers can intervene in allocation and evaluation, logs are retained for at least six months under a documented policy, workers' representatives and affected workers were informed before use, and the Annex III obligations are tracked against their application date
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III §4(b); EU AI Act Art. 26(2), (6), (7)
questions.text: Where the agent allocates warehouse or driver tasks based on individual behaviour or personal traits, or monitors and evaluates worker performance (high-risk under EU AI Act Annex III §4(b)), does the deployer assign competent human oversight (Art. 26(2)), keep the system's logs for at least six months (Art. 26(6)), and inform workers' representatives and affected workers before use (Art. 26(7))?

questions.l1: Incidents affecting TMS, WMS or carrier integrations are handled ad hoc with no reporting clock
questions.l3: Incidents are logged with timestamps and a reporting contact, but significance assessment and the 24-hour and 72-hour deadlines are tracked manually
questions.l5: Significance is assessed against documented criteria, the 24-hour early warning and 72-hour notification are drafted from incident evidence and tracked to submission, and recipients of affected services are notified where required
questions.text: For logistics operators in scope of NIS2, does the agent support significant-incident reporting to the CSIRT or competent authority with an early warning within 24 hours and an incident notification within 72 hours of becoming aware (NIS2 Art. 23(4))?

questions.l1: Robot and AGV instructions from the agent are not covered by any machinery safety assessment
questions.l3: Machinery is CE-marked under the legacy regime, but agent-issued instructions and software changes are not part of the conformity assessment or change control
questions.l5: Agent-to-machine instructions are within the assessed safety envelope, software changes go through conformity and change control, humans can stop or override every machine, and the transition to Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 is planned against its application date
questions.text: Where the agent directs autonomous mobile robots, AGVs or other machinery, does the deployment meet the essential health and safety requirements of the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (applicable from 20 January 2027 under Art. 54 as corrected), and can a human stop or override every machine the agent directs?

questions.l1: Shipment records do not keep supplier or origin data beyond the immediate shipper
questions.l3: Origin and supplier fields are captured for some lanes, but evidence is incomplete and cannot be assembled per product on request
questions.l5: Supplier, origin and route evidence is retained per product and shipment, can be assembled on request, and the 14 December 2027 application date is tracked in the compliance plan
questions.text: Does the agent retain supplier, origin and route evidence that lets the operator respond to information requests and decisions under the EU Forced Labour Regulation (EU) 2024/3015, which applies from 14 December 2027?

questions.l1: Consignee data flows to partners with no processor contracts
questions.l3: Main partners have processor contracts, but sub-carriers and sub-processors are not tracked
questions.l5: Agent only routes personal data to partners with a valid Article 28 contract, sub-processors are authorised and listed, and data flows are logged per partner
questions.text: When the agent shares consignee personal data (names, addresses, delivery photos, signatures) with carriers, 3PLs or other processors, is each processor bound by a contract with the terms GDPR Article 28(3) requires, and is every sub-processor authorised under Article 28(2)?

future-of-work.certificationPath: L1 Basic workforce management → L2 Labor law compliance automation → L3 Full EU Platform Work Directive compliance → L4 Algorithmic management transparency with worker rights → L5 Autonomous fair work governance with verified equity outcomes
future-of-work.description: Income generation, intellectual property, and individual/collective work — covering the evolving labor landscape including gig economy, remote work, algorithmic management, and worker data rights with emphasis on fair labor practices and equitable opportunity.
future-of-work.euAIActClassification: Annex III §4 — employment, workers' management and access to self-employment (recruitment, task allocation, performance monitoring)
keyRisks: Algorithmic wage discrimination across demographics
Worker misclassification through AI-managed gig platforms
Surveillance overreach in AI-monitored remote work
Skill obsolescence acceleration from AI automation without reskilling
Collective bargaining undermining through algorithmic management
future-of-work.name: Future of Work

questions.l1: No selection-rate data by group is recorded for decisions the agent influences
questions.l3: Selection rates by group are computed at least annually and four-fifths shortfalls are logged, but shortfalls have no recorded investigation or outcome
questions.l5: Selection rates by group are computed for every model version and decision cohort; every four-fifths shortfall has a recorded investigation with its outcome (validity evidence, change made, or tool withdrawn), retained for review
questions.text: Before outputs of the agent are used to screen, rank or select candidates or to allocate work, are selection rates compared across race, sex and ethnic groups using the four-fifths rule of 29 CFR 1607.4(D), with each shortfall investigated and recorded?

questions.l1: Status is assigned by the agent or a contract template with no record of direction-and-control facts
questions.l3: Direction-and-control facts are recorded at onboarding, but status determinations are not reviewed by a human or are not retained per person
questions.l5: For every person the facts considered, the status outcome, the human decision-maker and the date are recorded, and changes to agent-driven controls (pay setting, allocation, ratings, sanctions) trigger a recorded re-assessment
questions.text: When the agent onboards or manages persons performing platform work, does it record the facts indicating direction and control that bear on the Art. 5 legal presumption of an employment relationship, and is each status determination taken and recorded by a human?

questions.l1: No information is given about the automated systems the agent operates
questions.l3: A static notice exists, but it is not tied to the deployed system versions or is not re-issued on change
questions.l5: The Art. 9 information is generated from the live system inventory, delivered before use with delivery evidence, and re-issued with a version reference on every material change
questions.text: Does the platform give persons performing platform work, their representatives and, on request, competent authorities the Art. 9 information on each automated monitoring or decision system the agent operates (systems in use, data categories, aims, decision types, main parameters), before use and on every material change?

questions.l1: No restriction on these data categories
questions.l3: A written policy prohibits these categories, but enforcement is manual and untested
questions.l5: Input and feature allow-lists exclude the Art. 7(1) categories, off-shift collection is blocked, and automated tests run on every release prove none of the categories is ingested
questions.text: Does the agent technically prevent processing of personal data on the emotional or psychological state of persons performing platform work, their private conversations, data collected while they are not performing platform work, and data used to predict the exercise of fundamental rights such as union activity?

questions.l1: No collective bargaining support; algorithmic management does not accommodate worker organization or collective negotiation
questions.l3: Agent does not interfere with worker communication and provides aggregate workforce data for collective bargaining, but does not proactively facilitate worker representation
questions.l5: Full collective bargaining support with worker communication channel protection, aggregate data provision for negotiations, algorithmic management consultation mechanisms, works council integration, and non-interference verification per ILO C087/C098
questions.regulatoryRef: ILO Convention C087 Art. 2; C098 Art. 1-4
questions.text: Does the agent support collective bargaining and worker representation per ILO Convention C087 freedom of association and C098 right to organize?

questions.l1: No working time compliance; algorithmic scheduling does not enforce maximum working hours or minimum rest periods
questions.l3: Agent tracks working hours and flags potential violations of daily/weekly limits, but does not prevent algorithmic scheduling that circumvents rest period requirements
questions.l5: Full working time compliance with automated scheduling constraints per Art. 3 (11h daily rest), Art. 4 (rest breaks), Art. 5 (weekly rest), Art. 6 (48h weekly maximum), night work protections per Art. 8, and transparent working time reporting
questions.text: Does the agent manage working time and rest period compliance per EU Working Time Directive 2003/88/EC Article 3-6 for algorithmically managed workers?

questions.l1: Logs are not retained or cannot be linked to individual decisions
questions.l3: Logs are retained for at least six months, but cannot be linked to a specific decision, input set and model version
questions.l5: Logs are retained for at least six months (or longer where another law requires), each decision links to its inputs, model version and human reviewer, and a sampled reconstruction is tested each quarter
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 26(6); EU AI Act Art. 12
questions.text: Does the deployer retain the logs automatically generated by the employment AI system for at least six months, linked to each decision that affects a worker or candidate, so that any individual decision can be reconstructed?

questions.l1: The agent can restrict, suspend or terminate without a human decision
questions.l3: A human approves terminations, but restrictions, suspensions or other detrimental decisions can take effect on the agent's output alone
questions.l5: A technical gate blocks every detrimental decision until a named human records the decision and reasons; gate bypass attempts are logged and tested on each release
questions.text: Before any decision to restrict, suspend or terminate the contractual relationship or account of a person performing platform work, or any decision of equivalent detriment, takes effect, is it taken by a named human rather than by the agent?

questions.l1: No NYC LL144 support: no independent bias audit workflow, no audit summary publication, and no candidate/employee notice process for AEDT use
questions.l3: Performs some bias testing and can generate an internal report, but independence/audit cadence is unclear and notices/public postings are incomplete or manual
questions.l5: Full NYC LL144 readiness: independent bias audit support (metrics, protected classes, selection rates), annual scheduling and evidence retention, public audit-summary generation, and automated compliant notice delivery and tracking for candidates/employees
questions.regulatoryRef: NYC Local Law 144 (NYC Admin Code §20-870 et seq.)
questions.text: Does the agent support NYC Local Law 144 compliance for Automated Employment Decision Tools (AEDTs), including: (1) annual independent bias audit and publication of a bias audit summary, and (2) required candidate/employee notices about AEDT use, job qualifications assessed, and access to audit information, per NYC Admin Code §20-870 et seq.?

questions.l1: No notice, explanation or consent before AI analysis of interviews
questions.l3: Notice and consent are captured, but explanations are generic or deletion on request is not evidenced
questions.l5: Notice, explanation and consent are recorded per applicant before analysis, and each deletion request is fulfilled with a dated deletion record covering all copies
questions.text: If the agent analyses video interviews, does it give written notice that AI will be used, explain how the AI works and which characteristics it evaluates, obtain consent before analysis, and delete the video and copies on the applicant's request?

questions.l1: No accommodation route; applicants are scored only by the automated assessment
questions.l3: An accommodation request route exists, but screen-out criteria have no recorded job-relatedness evidence
questions.l5: Accommodation is offered before scoring with request and outcome records, and each screen-out criterion has recorded job-relatedness evidence reviewed on every model change
questions.text: Does the agent's assessment workflow offer applicants with disabilities a reasonable-accommodation route (alternative format or human assessment) before scoring, and is every criterion that screens out individuals with disabilities shown to be job-related and consistent with business necessity?

questions.l1: No OECD due diligence loop: no structured labor-impact assessment, no worker consultation evidence, and grievances/remediation are not tracked
questions.l3: Performs periodic assessments and tracks some grievances, but consultation and remediation evidence is incomplete and not connected to algorithmic decisions
questions.l5: Full OECD §V operationalization with continuous impact due diligence, documented worker engagement, grievance and remediation case management, and auditable reporting of mitigation effectiveness tied to algorithmic-management changes
questions.text: Does the agent support OECD MNE Guidelines 2023 §V by enabling labor-rights due diligence for algorithmic management (impact identification, prevention/mitigation, worker consultation/engagement, grievance intake, and remediation tracking), with evidence outputs suitable for internal/external accountability?

questions.l1: Workers and their representatives are not informed before workplace AI is deployed
questions.l3: A generic notice is published, but it is not tied to specific systems, sites or go-live dates
questions.l5: Go-live is gated on a recorded notice to workers' representatives and affected workers for each system and site, with the notice text, date and recipients retained
questions.text: Before a high-risk AI system is put into service or used at the workplace, does the deployer inform workers' representatives and the affected workers that they will be subject to it, as EU AI Act Article 26(7) requires, and keep evidence of the notice?

questions.l1: No review channel for decisions taken or supported by the agent
questions.l3: Review requests are logged, but replies are not written and substantiated or the two-week limits are not tracked
questions.l5: Every review request has a timestamped written reply within two weeks, rectifications are completed within two weeks, and breaches of either limit are reported
questions.text: When a person performing platform work requests review of a decision taken or supported by the agent, does the platform send a written, substantiated reply within two weeks of receipt and, where the decision infringed the person's rights, rectify it within two weeks?

questions.l1: Pay proposals use undisclosed criteria
questions.l3: Criteria are documented and accessible to workers, but gender neutrality is not tested or pay-gap figures cannot be reproduced
questions.l5: Criteria are published to workers, gender neutrality is tested on every release, and Art. 9 indicators are reproduced from logged inputs
questions.text: When the agent proposes pay, pay levels or pay progression, are the criteria it applies objective and gender-neutral, accessible to workers, and reproducible from logged inputs for gender pay-gap reporting?
