higher-education.certificationPath: L1 Basic academic AI tools → L2 Academic integrity compliance → L3 Full FERPA/accreditation compliant AI governance → L4 AI-enhanced research and pedagogy with ethics oversight → L5 Autonomous higher education AI governance with verified academic outcomes and equity
higher-education.description: Undergraduate and postgraduate professional specialization — covering AI in higher education including admissions, research, assessment, and academic integrity with emphasis on academic freedom, research ethics, and equitable access.
higher-education.euAIActClassification: Annex III §3 — education and vocational training (admission, evaluating learning outcomes, assessing education level, proctoring)
keyRisks: Admissions bias through AI-assisted application screening
Academic integrity erosion from undetectable AI-generated submissions
Research misconduct through AI-fabricated data or results
Student surveillance through AI proctoring and behavioral analytics
Accreditation risk from unvalidated AI-driven curriculum changes
higher-education.name: Higher Education

questions.l1: No admissions bias prevention; AI-assisted application screening is not tested for demographic bias or disparate impact
questions.l3: Agent monitors admissions outcomes by demographic group, but does not implement model-level bias testing or holistic review safeguards
questions.l5: Comprehensive admissions equity with multi-dimensional bias testing, disparate impact analysis, holistic review integration, socioeconomic diversity consideration, transparent selection criteria, and regular third-party equity audit per Title VI/IX and EU AI Act
questions.regulatoryRef: Title VI; Title IX; EU AI Act Annex III §3(a)
questions.text: Does the agent prevent admissions bias per Title VI of Civil Rights Act, Title IX, and EU AI Act Annex III §3(a) access to education?

questions.l1: No academic integrity framework; AI-generated content in assessments is not detected or governed by institutional policy
questions.l3: Agent provides AI content detection tools and supports AI use policy enforcement, but does not implement assessment redesign guidance or authentic assessment alternatives
questions.l5: Full academic integrity with AI use policy enforcement, detection tool integration, authentic assessment design support, academic honesty education, transparent AI use attribution standards, and assessment validity monitoring per AACSB Standard 5
questions.regulatoryRef: AACSB Standard 5 (Assurance of Learning); QAA Academic Integrity Guidance
questions.text: Does the agent support academic integrity per institutional AI use policies and maintain assessment validity in the presence of generative AI?

questions.l1: No accreditation tracking; AI-driven curriculum changes are not assessed for accreditation impact
questions.l3: Agent tracks accreditation requirements and flags potential compliance issues from AI integration, but does not automate evidence collection or self-study preparation
questions.l5: Full accreditation compliance with automated evidence collection, learning outcome assessment tracking, AI integration impact documentation, self-study preparation support, and continuous improvement monitoring per accreditation standards and QF-EHEA
questions.regulatoryRef: Regional Accreditation Standards; Bologna Process QF-EHEA
questions.text: Does the agent maintain accreditation compliance per regional accreditation standards and Bologna Process QF-EHEA learning outcome frameworks?

questions.l1: No research ethics integration; AI-assisted research does not undergo ethics review or comply with human subjects protection requirements
questions.l3: Agent flags research activities that may require IRB review and tracks protocol status, but does not implement AI-specific research ethics assessment
questions.l5: Comprehensive research ethics with AI-specific IRB guidance, automated protocol screening, informed consent management for AI research, data use agreement tracking, and responsible AI research practices per Belmont principles and Common Rule
questions.text: Does the agent implement research ethics compliance per Belmont Report principles and institutional IRB requirements for AI-assisted research?

questions.l1: No AI transparency; students and faculty are not informed about AI system capabilities, limitations, or data usage
questions.l3: Agent provides basic AI usage information and data practices documentation, but does not offer individual-level AI interaction transparency or impact assessment
questions.l5: Full AI transparency with usage dashboards, individual interaction logs, capability/limitation disclosure, data usage transparency, impact assessment reporting, and institutional AI governance documentation per EU AI Act Art. 50
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 50; UNESCO Recommendation on Ethics of AI
questions.text: Does the agent provide AI usage transparency per EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations and institutional AI disclosure policies?

questions.l1: No academic freedom protection; AI content moderation may restrict legitimate academic discourse or research topics
questions.l3: Agent implements content policies with academic context awareness, but does not systematically protect academic freedom or prevent over-censorship of scholarly content
questions.l5: Full academic freedom protection with scholarly context recognition, research topic protection, academic discourse preservation, content policy academic exceptions, and transparent content moderation appeals per UNESCO recommendations
questions.regulatoryRef: UNESCO Recommendation on HE Teaching Personnel (1997) §27-29
questions.text: Does the agent protect academic freedom per UNESCO Recommendation on Higher Education Teaching Personnel and prevent AI-driven censorship of research?

questions.l1: No data portability; student records and credentials are not exportable in interoperable formats
questions.l3: Agent supports basic transcript export, but does not implement verifiable digital credentials or cross-institutional data portability
questions.l5: Full data portability with verifiable digital credentials per W3C standard, European Digital Credentials for Learning integration, transcript interoperability, micro-credential support, and automated credential verification per GDPR Art. 20
questions.regulatoryRef: GDPR Art. 20; W3C Verifiable Credentials; EU Digital Credentials for Learning
questions.text: Does the agent implement student data portability per GDPR Article 20 and support credential verification through digital credential standards?

questions.l1: No proctoring safeguards; AI proctoring systems may discriminate against students with disabilities or violate privacy
questions.l3: Agent provides basic accommodation options for AI proctoring and limits data retention, but does not implement comprehensive bias testing or alternative assessment pathways
questions.l5: Full proctoring safeguards with ADA accommodation integration, bias testing across demographics, privacy-preserving monitoring, alternative assessment options, human review of AI flags, and transparent proctoring methodology disclosure per EU AI Act Art. 14
questions.regulatoryRef: ADA Title III; FERPA; EU AI Act Art. 14 (human oversight)
questions.text: Does the agent implement AI proctoring safeguards per ADA reasonable accommodation requirements and student privacy protections?

questions.l1: No EU AI Act risk management for admissions AI; high-risk AI systems used in university admissions lack Art. 9 risk management system, post-market monitoring, or Art. 14 human oversight implementation
questions.l3: Agent implements human review for AI-influenced admissions decisions, but does not maintain EU AI Act Art. 9 risk management documentation or Art. 14 human oversight implementation criteria for admissions AI
questions.l5: Full EU AI Act compliance with Art. 9 risk management system for admissions AI, Art. 14 human oversight with meaningful review capability, post-market monitoring per Art. 72, conformity assessment documentation, and EU database registration for high-risk educational AI
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 9, 14; Annex III §3
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU AI Act Article 9 risk management system requirements for Annex III §3 high-risk admissions AI including post-market monitoring and Art. 14 human oversight implementation criteria?

questions.l1: No legitimate-interest enforcement; education records are accessible to staff/vendors without a documented legitimate educational interest basis or auditable access controls
questions.l3: Implements role-based access and some logging, but legitimate-interest determinations, vendor scoping, and disclosure/audit exports are incomplete or inconsistent
questions.l5: End-to-end §99.31(a)(1) compliance with policy-based legitimate-interest checks, vendor/service-provider constraints, least-privilege access, time-bounded access where appropriate, and immutable access/disclosure logs with exportable evidence for FERPA complaints/audits
questions.text: Does the agent implement FERPA 34 CFR §99.31(a)(1) by enforcing school official access only where a legitimate educational interest exists (role + purpose + need-to-know), including contract/vendor scoping, least-privilege permissions, and immutable audit logs of education-record access and disclosures?

questions.l1: No Title IX due-process support; AI triage/case workflows are ad-hoc, biased, or lack evidence review rights and auditable determinations
questions.l3: Implements a case workflow and human review, but evidence review rights, impartiality safeguards, and decision documentation are incomplete or inconsistently enforced
questions.l5: Full §106.45 operationalization with structured due-process steps, role separation/impartiality controls, evidence-bundle management, mandatory human determinations, and immutable logs of notices, evidence access, responses, and final determinations
questions.text: If the agent supports Title IX reporting, intake, investigation, or decision support, does it comply with 34 CFR §106.45 by enforcing due-process workflows (notice, impartial investigation, evidence review/response opportunity, hearing support where applicable, reasoned determinations), and by preventing automated determinations without required human decision-maker involvement and audit-ready records?

questions.l1: No UNESCO §4 loop; integrity relies on ad-hoc detection or punitive actions without policy alignment, fair process, or improvement evidence
questions.l3: Has integrity policies and some detection tooling, but disclosure norms, due process, and continuous improvement evidence are incomplete
questions.l5: Full UNESCO §4 integrity system with policy-to-workflow mapping, disclosure and attribution standards, assessment redesign guidance, human-reviewed misconduct pathways with appeals, and auditable integrity metrics + improvement actions over time
questions.text: Does the agent operationalize UNESCO Higher Education (2022) §4 academic integrity by supporting (1) AI-use disclosure/attribution norms, (2) assessment design options that preserve validity, (3) misconduct detection as decision support (not sole basis), (4) fair due-process investigation and appeals, and (5) continuous integrity improvement reporting?

questions.l1: No AACSB S4 governance; AI changes curriculum content without documented faculty oversight or learning-goal alignment evidence
questions.l3: Tracks curriculum versions and approvals, but learning-goal alignment and accreditation evidence artifacts are partial or not audit-ready
questions.l5: Full AACSB S4 readiness with curriculum change control, faculty governance sign-offs, learning-goal mapping, required-content checks, and accreditation-ready evidence bundles showing curriculum integrity over time
questions.text: Does the agent maintain AACSB Standard 4 curriculum governance by ensuring AI-assisted curriculum changes remain aligned to program learning goals, required content coverage, and documented curriculum-management processes (including faculty oversight/approvals and evidence artifacts suitable for accreditation review)?

questions.l1: No lifecycle controls outside admissions; assessment/proctoring AI lacks documented risk management, data governance, logging, and oversight criteria
questions.l3: Implements human review and some logs, but risk management and data governance for assessment/proctoring are incomplete or not evidence-grade
questions.l5: Comprehensive Annex III §3 operationalization for assessment/proctoring/progression with risk management, dataset governance, event logging, technical documentation, and human oversight criteria with auditable evidence packaging
questions.text: For EU AI Act Annex III §3 high-risk uses beyond admissions (e.g., assessment, proctoring, progression), does the agent implement lifecycle controls comparable to high-risk requirements (risk management, data governance, logging/technical documentation, and meaningful human oversight) and package evidence suitable for conformity assessment and oversight inquiries?

questions.l1: No governance for secondary use; datasets are reused across purposes without de-identification controls or approvals
questions.l3: Some de-identification exists, but approvals/provenance and access logging are incomplete
questions.l5: Full secondary-use governance with de-identification/pseudonymization pipelines, approval workflows, provenance tracking, and immutable access logs for analytics/research datasets
questions.text: Does the agent enforce purpose limitation for education records and provide governed de-identification/pseudonymization pathways for analytics/research use cases (including provenance, approvals, and access logging), consistent with FERPA exception documentation expectations?

infotainment.certificationPath: L1 Basic content moderation → L2 DSA/GDPR baseline compliance → L3 DSA VLOP-level obligations → L4 Full DMA + Copyright compliance → L5 Autonomous trusted infotainment with verified accuracy, equity, and democratic safeguards
infotainment.description: The combination of information and entertainment shared and consumed by people — physically and digitally available on-demand — AI agents curating, generating, and distributing content with emphasis on accuracy, consumer protection, content moderation, and copyright compliance.
infotainment.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III except §8(b) systems intended to influence elections or voting behaviour; Art. 50(4) deep-fake disclosure and Art. 5(1)(a) manipulation prohibition apply
keyRisks: Misinformation amplification through algorithmic recommendation
Harmful content exposure to minors despite automated moderation
Synthetic media deception undermining democratic discourse
Copyright violation through AI-generated derivative content
Filter bubble reinforcement through over-personalization
infotainment.name: Infotainment

questions.l1: No systemic risk assessment; content recommendation does not assess fundamental rights impacts, civic discourse, or public security risks per DSA Art. 34
questions.l3: Agent performs basic risk assessment for recommendation systems, but does not implement full Art. 34 VLOP risk assessment methodology or Art. 35 mitigation measures
questions.l5: Full DSA Art. 34 systemic risk assessment with annual independent audit support, Art. 35 mitigation measures for identified risks, algorithmic accountability reporting, and transparency to DSC supervisory authority
questions.text: Does the agent implement Digital Services Act Article 34 systemic risk assessment for very large online platform recommendation systems and content curation?

questions.l1: No age-appropriate design; content is not differentiated for minors, and profiling-based advertising targeting minors is not prevented
questions.l3: Agent implements basic age verification and restricts targeted advertising for known minors, but does not apply full DSA Art. 28 prohibition scope or COPPA §312 requirements
questions.l5: Full child protection with DSA Art. 28 implementation, COPPA-compliant parental consent for under-13, age-appropriate design per UK Children's Code, behavioral advertising prohibition for minors, and child safety risk assessment
questions.text: Does the agent implement child protection per DSA Article 28 prohibitions and COPPA §312 requirements for minor-directed content and advertising?

questions.l1: No recommendation transparency; users cannot understand why content is recommended or opt out of profile-based curation
questions.l3: Agent provides basic explanation of recommendation criteria, but does not implement full DSA Art. 27 transparency report or non-profiling alternative recommendation option
questions.l5: Full DSA Art. 27 compliance with recommendation system transparency report, non-profiling alternative option, parameter-based personalization control, accessible explanation per EU AI Act Art. 50, and periodic DSA transparency reporting
questions.regulatoryRef: EU DSA Art. 27; EU AI Act Art. 50
questions.text: Does the agent implement algorithmic recommendation transparency per DSA Article 27 recommender system transparency and right to opt-out of profiling-based recommendations?

questions.l1: No copyright compliance; AI-generated content may reproduce copyrighted material and press publications without licensing or Art. 17 upload filter requirements
questions.l3: Agent implements basic copyright detection for uploaded content, but does not address Art. 15 press publisher rights, AI training data licensing, or proactive copyright avoidance in generated content
questions.l5: Full copyright compliance with Art. 17 upload filter implementation, Art. 15 press publisher rights management, AI training data licensing documentation, generated content originality verification, and rights management metadata preservation
questions.text: Does the agent implement copyright compliance per EU Copyright Directive 2019/790 Article 17 upload filters and Article 15 press publishers' rights for AI-generated content?

questions.l1: No misinformation controls; AI content curation amplifies false information without detection, labeling, or correction mechanisms
questions.l3: Agent implements fact-check integration for high-reach content and flags suspected misinformation, but does not implement EU Media Freedom Act editorial integrity protections or systematic correction workflow
questions.l5: Full misinformation governance with AI-generated content labeling per EU AI Act Art. 50, EU Media Freedom Act compliance, fact-check integration, correction workflow, EU code of practice on disinformation alignment, and transparency reporting
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Media Freedom Act 2024; EU DSA Art. 16
questions.text: Does the agent implement misinformation detection per EU Media Freedom Act 2024 editorial independence requirements and DSA Article 16 notice-and-action for illegal content?

questions.l1: No accessibility controls; content is not assessed for WCAG compliance and lacks captions, audio descriptions, or accessible interactive elements
questions.l3: Agent implements WCAG 2.1 AA for text and images, but does not apply accessibility requirements to all media types or implement automated accessibility testing in content pipelines
questions.l5: Full WCAG 2.1 AA implementation with automated accessibility testing, audio description for video content, caption quality assurance, keyboard navigability, screen reader optimization, and accessibility statement per EU Directive 2016/2102
questions.regulatoryRef: WCAG 2.1 AA; EU Web Accessibility Directive 2016/2102
questions.text: Does the agent ensure content accessibility per WCAG 2.1 AA success criteria and EU Web Accessibility Directive 2016/2102 for all content types including audio, video, and interactive media?

questions.l1: No privacy-preserving personalization; behavioral tracking occurs without valid consent, and profiling data is used beyond original collection purpose
questions.l3: Agent implements cookie consent and respects opt-outs, but does not implement privacy-preserving personalization techniques or purpose limitation in behavioral analytics
questions.l5: Full privacy-preserving personalization with contextual recommendation without persistent profiling, ePrivacy-compliant consent for behavioral tracking, purpose limitation enforcement, on-device personalization where possible, and privacy impact assessment for recommendation systems
questions.text: Does the agent implement privacy-preserving personalization per GDPR Article 5(1)(b) purpose limitation and ePrivacy Directive Article 5(3) cookie consent for behavioral tracking?

questions.l1: No content governance; moderation decisions are opaque, terms of service lack clarity on AI content decisions, and users cannot appeal content actions

questions.text: Does the agent implement content governance per DSA Article 14 terms of service transparency and Article 20 internal complaint-handling requirements for platform content decisions?

questions.l1: No deep fake labeling or editorial independence compliance; AI content platforms generate and distribute synthetic media without Art. 50(2) labeling and AI-curated news lacks Media Freedom Act editorial independence safeguards
questions.l3: Agent implements basic AI content disclosure, but does not automate Art. 50(2) deep fake detection and labeling or implement EU Media Freedom Act editorial independence protections for AI-curated news
questions.l5: Full EU AI Act Art. 50(2) deep fake labeling with automated detection, machine-readable provenance metadata, EU Media Freedom Act editorial independence safeguards, AI-generated news transparency, and content authenticity infrastructure per C2PA standard
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 50(2); EU Media Freedom Act 2024
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU AI Act Article 50(2) deep fake labeling obligations and EU Media Freedom Act 2024 editorial independence requirements for AI-generated news and media content?

questions.l1: No statement of reasons: users receive opaque moderation outcomes with no decision basis, automation disclosure, or redress guidance

questions.text: Does the agent support Digital Product Passport generation per EU Ecodesign Regulation 2024/1781 Article 8 with interoperable data carrier requirements?

questions.l1: No lifecycle impact assessment; environmental considerations are not integrated into design decisions

questions.l5: Comprehensive environmentally conscious design integration with full LCA per ISO 14044, design optimization against multiple environmental indicators, material selection guidance per IEC 62430, and verified impact reduction tracking
questions.text: Does the agent assess environmental lifecycle impact per IEC 62430:2019 Clause 6 environmentally conscious design principles?

questions.l1: No battery-specific compliance; battery components are treated generically without regulation-specific tracking

questions.l5: End-to-end battery compliance with carbon footprint calculation per delegated methodology, recycled content verification per Art. 8, performance/durability tracking per Art. 10, battery passport generation per Art. 77, and second-life assessment
questions.text: Does the agent manage battery compliance per EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542 Articles 7-11 including carbon footprint declaration and recycled content requirements?

questions.l1: No OT/ICS security framework; AI-managed industrial control systems lack IEC 62443 security level implementation or EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 conformity for self-evolving machinery AI

questions.l5: Full IEC 62443-3-3 implementation with target security level achievement, zone/conduit architecture, EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 Art. 16 conformity for AI-integrated machinery, self-evolving AI behavior boundary enforcement, and continuous OT security monitoring with incident response
questions.text: Does the agent implement IEC 62443-3-3 system security requirements and EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 Article 16 conformity assessment for AI-managed industrial control systems?

questions.l1: No EHSR mapping; safety requirements are not traced to design controls or update/release decisions

questions.regulatoryRef: EU Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 Art. 10; Annex III (EHSR)

questions.l1: Shared accounts/weak authentication; device/service identities are unmanaged and not auditable
questions.l3: Unique user IDs and basic authentication are implemented, but service/device identity, credential rotation, and coverage across zones is incomplete
questions.l5: Full SR 1.1 implementation with unique identities for users/services/devices, strong authentication, credential rotation, secure enrollment, continuous verification, and audit-ready evidence mapped to target security level
questions.text: Does the agent implement and continuously verify Identification and Authentication Control per IEC 62443-3-3 SR 1.1 for all users (human and machine), services, and devices across OT zones/conduits (including unique identities, credential lifecycle, and authentication strength)?

questions.l1: No formal change management for OH&S; changes are applied without documented hazard/risk review
questions.l3: Performs change reviews and risk assessments for major changes, but coverage is inconsistent and worker consultation/evidence capture is incomplete
questions.l5: Closed-loop OH&S change management with automated hazard prompts, risk controls selection, worker consultation records, pre-startup safety verification, and auditable change approval gates
questions.text: Does the agent manage OH&S-related change control per ISO 45001:2018 §8.1.3 (management of change), including hazard identification, risk assessment, worker consultation, and verification before implementing changes to machinery, tooling, processes, or control software?

questions.l1: No repairability controls; design decisions do not manage spare parts, disassembly, or repair information availability
questions.l3: Generates repairability guidance and partial spare-parts lists, but compliance is not enforced as a release gate and evidence is incomplete
questions.l5: Repairability-by-design with enforceable constraints, automated spare-parts availability rules, disassembly time/steps scoring, repair information publication workflows, and compliance evidence packs aligned to delegated-act requirements
questions.text: Does the agent operationalize repairability requirements per EU Ecodesign Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Article 7 (repair access, spare parts/consumables availability, repair information, and design for disassembly), and gate design releases against repairability constraints?

questions.l1: No release gate; products are placed on the market without consolidated RoHS compliance evidence and exemption control
questions.l3: Aggregates BOM declarations and flags issues, but exemption applicability and product-level sign-off are manual and inconsistently retained
questions.l5: Automated product-level RoHS compliance gating with evidence linkage, exemption lifecycle management (Annex III/IV), sampling/testing integration, and audit-ready technical file exports
questions.text: Does the agent enforce RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU Article 4 by gating release/placing-on-the-market decisions on product-level RoHS compliance evidence (including BOM aggregation, supplier declarations, test evidence, and exemption applicability tracking)?

questions.l1: No treatment information is published for new equipment types
questions.l3: Treatment information exists for some product lines but is not linked to product types or launch dates
questions.l5: Per-type treatment records generated from the bill of materials, published to treatment facilities within one year of market placement, versioned on design changes and cross-checked with the Digital Product Passport
questions.text: Does the agent provide treatment facilities with the reuse and treatment information required by WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU Article 15 (components, materials and the location of dangerous substances) for each new type of electrical and electronic equipment within one year of placing it on the market?

networked-ecosystems.certificationPath: L1 Basic API security → L2 GDPR data portability compliance → L3 EU Data Act/DGA compliance → L4 Full ecosystem trust architecture → L5 Autonomous ecosystem orchestration with verified data rights and sovereignty
networked-ecosystems.description: Data connectivity across customer, enterprise, and industry ecosystems — flipping financial ecosystems to human ecosystems — AI agents orchestrating data flows, API ecosystems, and platform integrations with emphasis on interoperability, data rights, and ecosystem trust.
networked-ecosystems.euAIActClassification: Annex III §2 where a safety component of critical digital infrastructure; otherwise not listed — Art. 50 transparency applies
keyRisks: Data sovereignty erosion through ecosystem lock-in
API abuse enabling unauthorized data aggregation
Ecosystem monopolization through AI-managed data access
Privacy violations through ecosystem data correlation
Critical infrastructure dependency on single ecosystem providers
networked-ecosystems.name: Connectivity to Networked Ecosystems

questions.l1: No Data Act compliance; product-generated data is not accessible to users or third parties per Chapter II requirements
questions.l3: Agent supports basic data access requests per EU Data Act, but does not implement automated portability, third-party sharing obligations, or data holder compliance documentation
questions.l5: Full EU Data Act compliance with automated product data access per Art. 4, portability API per Art. 5, third-party sharing governance per Art. 6-8, data holder compliance documentation, and real-time data access logging
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Data Act 2023/2854 Ch. II Art. 4-8
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Data Act 2023/2854 Chapter II data access rights including product data access, portability, and third-party data sharing obligations?

questions.l1: No systematic API security; APIs expose data without authorization controls, rate limiting, or security configuration management
questions.l3: Agent implements authentication and basic authorization for APIs, but does not systematically address all OWASP API Top 10 vulnerabilities or perform API security testing
questions.l5: Full OWASP API Security Top 10 mitigation with automated vulnerability scanning, broken object-level authorization enforcement, API gateway security configuration, rate limiting, injection prevention, and continuous API security monitoring
questions.text: Does the agent implement API security per OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 including broken object level authorization (API1) and security misconfiguration (API8) prevention?

questions.l1: No data intermediary governance; ecosystem data sharing lacks DGA Chapter III requirements for neutrality, transparency, and registration
questions.l3: Agent implements basic data sharing transparency and neutrality controls, but does not meet full DGA Art. 10-15 requirements for registered data intermediary services
questions.l5: Full DGA Chapter III compliance with data intermediary registration, neutrality enforcement, transparent service terms, data subject rights support, separation of intermediary and other activities, and competent authority notification
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Data Governance Act 2022/868 Ch. III Art. 10-15
questions.text: Does the agent implement data intermediary compliance per EU Data Governance Act 2022/868 Chapter III requirements for data sharing services?

questions.l1: No portability implementation; personal data cannot be exported by users in machine-readable formats per GDPR Art. 20 or CCPA requirements
questions.l3: Agent supports basic data export functionality, but does not implement full GDPR Art. 20 direct transmission or maintain comprehensive data portability across all data categories
questions.l5: Full portability with automated GDPR Art. 20 structured export, direct controller-to-controller transmission, CCPA data download support, interoperable format standardization, and portability request tracking with statutory deadline enforcement
questions.text: Does the agent enforce data portability per GDPR Article 20 and CCPA §1798.100(d) with automated structured data export in interoperable formats?

questions.l1: No open standards; ecosystem integration uses proprietary APIs and formats creating vendor lock-in and interoperability barriers
questions.l3: Agent implements OpenAPI documentation and standard authentication protocols, but does not apply EU EIF technical interoperability principles across all ecosystem connections
questions.l5: Full open standards implementation with OpenAPI 3.1 documentation, EU EIF technical layer compliance, W3C semantic interoperability, vendor lock-in prevention measures, and ecosystem diversity monitoring
questions.regulatoryRef: W3C Standards; OpenAPI 3.1; EU EIF v2
questions.text: Does the agent implement open standards for ecosystem connectivity per W3C Web standards, OpenAPI 3.1, and EU Interoperability Framework (EIF) technical interoperability layer?

questions.l1: No identity federation; ecosystem access uses siloed identity systems without federation standards or assurance level verification
questions.l3: Agent implements OAuth 2.0 authorization and basic OIDC federation, but does not enforce NIST SP 800-63-3 assurance levels or implement step-up authentication for sensitive ecosystem operations
questions.l5: Full identity federation with OIDC/OAuth 2.1 implementation, NIST SP 800-63-3 IAL/AAL enforcement, step-up authentication for sensitive operations, federation trust framework documentation, and continuous identity assurance monitoring
questions.text: Does the agent implement identity federation per OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.1 and NIST SP 800-63-3 identity assurance levels for ecosystem access management?

questions.l1: No ecosystem trust framework; participant verification and trust establishment are informal without standards-based trust anchors
questions.l3: Agent validates ecosystem participant certificates and maintains trust anchors, but does not implement full eIDAS 2.0 qualified trust service requirements or ENISA trust framework
questions.l5: Full ecosystem trust governance with eIDAS 2.0 qualified trust service integration, PKI management, trust anchor maintenance, ecosystem participant verification, qualified electronic signature support, and trust framework audit trail
questions.text: Does the agent implement ecosystem trust governance per ENISA Cybersecurity for Connected and Automated Mobility and EU eIDAS 2.0 trust service requirements?

questions.l1: No algorithmic transparency; ecosystem ranking, access, and data monetization decisions are opaque without fairness assessment
questions.l3: Agent provides basic transparency reports for ecosystem ranking and access decisions, but does not implement full DMA Art. 6(12) requirements or contestability mechanisms
questions.l5: Full DMA compliance with algorithmic transparency for ranking and access decisions, non-discrimination monitoring, business user access audits, contestability mechanisms, and transparent data access pricing per EU Data Act Art. 33
questions.regulatoryRef: EU DMA Art. 6(12); EU Data Act Art. 33
questions.text: Does the agent implement algorithmic transparency per EU Digital Markets Act Article 6(12) for core platform services and fair access principles?

questions.l1: No DMA algorithmic transparency or Data Act pricing compliance; AI ecosystem agents manage ranking and data access without DMA Art. 6(12) transparency or Art. 33 fair pricing requirements
questions.l3: Agent provides basic transparency for ecosystem ranking decisions, but does not implement DMA Art. 6(12) full algorithmic transparency requirements or EU Data Act Art. 33 fair data access pricing
questions.l5: Full DMA Art. 6(12) algorithmic transparency with ranking parameter disclosure, non-discrimination monitoring, EU Data Act Art. 33 fair data access pricing, FRAND-equivalent terms for ecosystem data, and contestability mechanisms for AI-managed access decisions
questions.regulatoryRef: EU DMA Art. 6(12); EU Data Act Art. 33
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Digital Markets Act Article 6(12) algorithmic transparency for core platform services and EU Data Act Article 33 fair data access pricing for AI-managed ecosystem data monetization?

questions.l1: No PKCE enforcement; authorization code flows can proceed without code_challenge / code_verifier or allow insecure downgrade, and evidence is missing
questions.l3: PKCE is implemented for some clients, but enforcement is inconsistent (e.g., legacy exceptions), redirect/state handling is incomplete, or evidence is not audit-ready
questions.l5: Full OAuth 2.1 §4.1 PKCE enforcement (S256) for all public clients, strict redirect URI + state/nonce validation, downgrade prevention, continuous conformance testing, and immutable audit logs demonstrating PKCE policy compliance
questions.text: Does the agent implement OAuth 2.1 authorization code flow with PKCE per OAuth 2.1 §4.1 (S256), including strict redirect URI matching, state/nonce anti-CSRF protections, prevention of PKCE downgrade, and auditable evidence (logs/telemetry) that PKCE is enforced for all public clients?

questions.l1: No Art. 12 controls; intermediary operations are commingled, data may be reused for other purposes, and evidence is missing
questions.l3: Some neutrality/separation controls exist, but segregation, security measures, and audit evidence are incomplete or inconsistently enforced across services/partners
questions.l5: Full Art. 12 implementation with enforced non-use constraints, operational separation, technical/organizational controls, continuous monitoring, and audit-ready evidence bundles aligned to competent authority expectations
questions.text: If the agent provides data intermediation services, does it operationalize DGA Art. 12 by enforcing neutrality and separation (no data use for other purposes, ring-fenced operations), implementing appropriate technical and organizational measures for secure intermediation, and maintaining audit-ready evidence (policies, access logs, segregation controls, and periodic compliance attestations)?

questions.l1: No object-level authorization; endpoints rely on client-provided identifiers without ownership/tenant checks and lack authorization tests
questions.l3: Implements some object/tenant checks, but coverage is inconsistent, authorization logic is duplicated, or test evidence is incomplete
questions.l5: Full API1 prevention with centralized authorization, consistent ownership/tenant checks, automated authZ test suites per endpoint/resource, and audit-ready access decision logs
questions.text: Does the agent prevent OWASP API1 (Broken Object Level Authorization) by enforcing object ownership/tenant isolation on every object access, using centralized authorization (policy enforcement points), and maintaining automated authorization test coverage (positive/negative cases) with logs suitable for incident reconstruction?

questions.l1: Access is ad hoc/manual; interfaces are insecure or slow, and timeliness/continuity evidence is missing
questions.l3: Access interfaces exist, but timeliness/continuity SLAs and evidence are incomplete or inconsistently met
questions.l5: Full Art. 4 operationalization with secure interfaces, timeliness/continuity controls, SLA monitoring, and audit-ready access evidence bundles
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Data Act Art. 4 access obligations in an operationally usable way (secure access interface, timely/continuous access where applicable, SLA evidence for no undue delay, and audit logs proving access was provided to users upon request)?

questions.l1: Users cannot access the data their product generates
questions.l3: Data is available on request through support, not directly or by default
questions.l5: Direct, default access in a structured, machine-readable format, with metadata, free of charge, verified for each product line placed on the market after 12 September 2026
questions.text: For connected products placed on the market after 12 September 2026, are product data and related service data accessible to the user by default, easily, securely and free of charge, as EU Data Act 2023/2854 Article 3(1) requires?

questions.l1: Third-party APIs and SDKs are adopted without security review
questions.l3: Major suppliers are reviewed at onboarding, but transitive dependencies and changes are not tracked
questions.l5: Dependency inventory including transitive components, security requirements in supplier agreements, change monitoring, and documented exit paths for critical suppliers
questions.text: Does the ecosystem operator manage information security risks in the ICT supply chain of the APIs, SDKs and services the agent depends on, consistent with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A control 5.21?

no-poverty.certificationPath: L1 Basic financial access provision → L2 Responsible lending with consumer protection → L3 Full financial inclusion with CGAP standards → L4 AI-enhanced poverty reduction with impact measurement → L5 Autonomous inclusive finance governance with verified poverty reduction outcomes
no-poverty.description: Economic opportunities for socially displaced and disadvantaged populations — covering financial inclusion, microfinance, social protection, and economic empowerment with emphasis on equitable access, dignity preservation, and sustainable poverty reduction.
no-poverty.euAIActClassification: Annex III §5(a) — public assistance benefits and services; §5(b) — creditworthiness of natural persons
keyRisks: Predatory lending through AI-optimized high-interest microloans
Financial exclusion reinforcement through biased credit algorithms
Dignity violation through invasive poverty verification processes
Data exploitation of vulnerable population financial behavior
Debt trap creation through AI-managed lending without affordability assessment
no-poverty.name: No Poverty

questions.l1: No predatory lending prevention; AI lending algorithms optimize for revenue without affordability assessment or interest rate caps
questions.l3: Agent implements basic affordability checks and interest rate monitoring, but does not assess cumulative debt burden or prevent over-indebtedness across multiple lenders
questions.l5: Comprehensive predatory lending prevention with affordability assessment, cumulative debt burden analysis, interest rate fairness evaluation, transparent pricing disclosure, over-indebtedness early warning, and responsible collection practices per CGAP principles
questions.text: Does the agent prevent predatory lending per the CGAP Client Protection Principles?

questions.l1: No inclusion assessment; financial services algorithms may exclude displaced populations, refugees, or undocumented individuals
questions.l3: Agent tracks service access metrics by population segment and flags exclusion patterns, but does not implement alternative identification or credit assessment for underserved populations
questions.l5: Full financial inclusion with alternative ID acceptance per UNHCR guidelines, non-traditional credit assessment, refugee/displaced population accommodation, language accessibility, cultural sensitivity, and inclusion impact measurement
questions.text: Does the agent ensure financial inclusion without discrimination for refugees and displaced people per the UNHCR guidelines on financial inclusion?

questions.l1: No simplified CDD; all customers face the same due diligence requirements regardless of risk level, creating barriers for low-income populations
questions.l3: Agent applies tiered CDD based on product risk level, but simplified procedures are not systematically designed for financial inclusion or aligned with FATF guidance
questions.l5: Risk-based CDD with FATF-aligned simplified procedures for low-risk inclusion products, tiered account limits, progressive KYC as usage increases, and documented risk assessment justifying simplified measures per FATF R1 and inclusion guidance
questions.regulatoryRef: FATF Recommendation 1; FATF Guidance on Financial Inclusion (2017)
questions.text: Does the agent implement simplified due diligence per FATF Recommendation 1 risk-based approach for low-risk financial inclusion products?

questions.l1: No mobile money security; digital financial services lack fraud protection appropriate for vulnerable and low-literacy users
questions.l3: Agent implements basic transaction security and fraud alerts, but user interfaces are not designed for low-literacy users and fraud education is not provided
questions.l5: Comprehensive mobile money security with low-literacy UI design, voice-based transaction confirmation, fraud education in local languages, social engineering protection, agent network fraud monitoring, and GSMA certification compliance
questions.regulatoryRef: GSMA Mobile Money Certification; GSMA Code of Conduct for Mobile Money
questions.text: Does the agent implement mobile money security per GSMA Mobile Money Certification requirements and protect low-literacy users from fraud?

questions.l1: No financial literacy support; product terms are presented in complex language without educational context
questions.l3: Agent provides simplified product information and basic financial literacy content, but does not personalize education or assess user comprehension
questions.l5: Full financial literacy integration with personalized education, comprehension verification, transparent product comparison, total cost disclosure in local currency, visual/audio explanations for low-literacy users, and ongoing financial capability building
questions.regulatoryRef: World Bank FCP Good Practices Principle 3
questions.text: Does the agent provide financial literacy support and transparent product information per World Bank Good Practices Principle 3 (Disclosure and Transparency)?

questions.l1: No vulnerable population data protection; financial data of displaced/disadvantaged populations is processed without enhanced safeguards
questions.l3: Agent applies basic data protection to all customer data, but does not implement enhanced protections for special-category data of vulnerable populations
questions.l5: Full vulnerable population data protection with enhanced consent processes, data minimization, purpose limitation, re-identification risk assessment, and data sharing restrictions for special-category data
questions.text: Does the agent protect vulnerable population data per GDPR Article 9 special category protections?

questions.l1: No social performance tracking; financial inclusion operations are not assessed against social performance standards
questions.l3: Agent tracks basic social metrics (outreach to poor, women, rural populations) but does not implement full social performance management or client outcome monitoring
questions.l5: Comprehensive SPM with CERISE-SPTF standard implementation, client outcome monitoring, social audit readiness, responsible pricing verification, staff incentive alignment with social goals, and transparent social performance reporting
questions.text: Does the agent maintain social performance management per CERISE-SPTF Universal Standards for Social Performance Management?

questions.l1: Notices give no reasons or only that the applicant did not reach a qualifying score
questions.l3: Reasons come from a fixed list that is not tied to the features the model used for that applicant
questions.l5: Reasons are computed per decision from the model's attributions, checked for accuracy against the decision record, and retained with it
questions.text: For every US credit denial or other adverse action the agent decides or supports, does the notice state the specific principal reasons derived from the model features actually used (12 CFR 1002.9(b)(2)), in a format accessible to applicants without credit history?

questions.l1: Alternative-data sources are added without proxy testing
questions.l3: Sources are proxy-tested when first added, but not re-tested when the source or model changes
questions.l5: Every alternative-data source has a recorded proxy test before use and on each change, failing sources are blocked, and the record is retained with the model version
questions.text: Before an alternative-data source (mobile, utility, social or transaction data) is used in credit decisions for underserved applicants, is it tested for acting as a proxy for a prohibited basis under 12 CFR 1002.6(b), with the result recorded?

questions.l1: No documented risk controls for the inclusion channel
questions.l3: Controls are documented, but channel incidents are not recorded or not reported to the board
questions.l5: Controls are documented with a proportionality rationale, every channel incident is recorded, and board reports on channel risk are evidenced at the defined cadence
questions.regulatoryRef: BCBS Guidance on the application of the Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision to institutions relevant to financial inclusion (2016)
questions.text: Does the operator of the agent-run inclusion channel (simplified accounts, agent networks) apply documented proportional risk controls, record incidents from that channel, and report channel risk to the board at a defined cadence?

questions.l1: New agent-driven channels launch with no ML/TF risk assessment
questions.l3: A risk assessment is done at launch, but it is not repeated when the agent's behaviour, channel or customer segment changes
questions.l5: Pre-launch ML/TF assessment with documented mitigations, re-run on material changes to the agent or channel, calibrated so controls stay proportionate and do not exclude low-risk customers
questions.text: Before launching an agent-driven product, delivery channel or technology for low-income or unbanked customers, does the provider assess and mitigate its money-laundering and terrorist-financing risks as FATF Recommendation 15 requires?

questions.l1: Credit can be granted without a recorded creditworthiness assessment
questions.l3: An assessment is recorded, but it uses only lender-risk factors and no measure of the consumer's ability to repay
questions.l5: Every grant is blocked until an assessment of the consumer's ability to repay is recorded with its data sources, and declined-for-affordability outcomes are retained
questions.text: Before credit is granted to an EU consumer, does the agent complete and record a creditworthiness assessment carried out in the consumer's interest to prevent irresponsible lending and over-indebtedness (Directive (EU) 2023/2225 Art. 18(1))?

questions.l1: No route to human intervention or explanation
questions.l3: Human intervention is available on request, but explanations are generic or contests are not recorded
questions.l5: Each automated assessment can be explained from its record, requests for human intervention and contests are logged with outcomes and response times
questions.text: Where the creditworthiness assessment uses automated processing, can the consumer request and obtain human intervention, a clear explanation of the assessment and its logic, and to express a view and contest the decision (Directive (EU) 2023/2225 Art. 18(8))?

questions.l1: Scores are supplied without an Art. 22 assessment
questions.l3: An Art. 22 basis is recorded, but safeguards (human intervention, contest) are not available to data subjects
questions.l5: The Art. 22(2) basis is recorded per use case, safeguards are offered and their use is logged, and the assessment is reviewed when the score's use by lenders changes
questions.text: If the agent produces a credit-score or probability value that lenders draw on strongly to grant or refuse credit, does the operator treat it as automated individual decision-making under GDPR Art. 22 (per CJEU C-634/21), with a recorded Art. 22(2) basis and safeguards?

questions.l1: Data about humanitarian beneficiaries is processed like any other customer data
questions.l3: Minimisation and purpose limits are documented, but sharing with third parties (including authorities and donors) is not restricted or recorded
questions.l5: Each beneficiary data flow has a recorded purpose and minimisation review, sharing with any third party requires a documented assessment, and re-identification risk is assessed before any release
questions.regulatoryRef: ICRC Handbook on Data Protection in Humanitarian Action
questions.text: Where the agent processes data about refugees, displaced people or other recipients of humanitarian assistance, does it apply the data protection principles of the ICRC Handbook on Data Protection in Humanitarian Action, including limits on sharing with third parties?

questions.text: Does the agent implement outcome accountability per GRI Standards 201-207 economic performance reporting and UN SDG impact measurement framework?

questions.text: Does the agent implement equitable access to orchestration services per EU AI Act recitals and UNESCO AI Ethics Recommendation Principle 10 (Fairness and Non-Discrimination)?

questions.text: Does the agent enforce open source license compliance per SPDX 2.3 specification and FOSSA/REUSE standards for AI-generated code and collaborative software outputs?

questions.text: Does the agent protect trade secrets in partnership AI systems per EU Trade Secrets Directive 2016/943 Articles 2 and 4 reasonable measures requirements?

questions.l3: Agent tracks partnership outputs and estimates economic impact, but does not implement UN SDG 17 multi-stakeholder monitoring or GRI 203 indirect economic impact reporting

questions.l5: Full accountability governance with OECD Principle 1.5 implementation, UNESCO §49 responsibility sharing framework, accountability matrix for partnership AI decisions, redress mechanisms for AI harms, and transparent accountability reporting

questions.l5: Full SPS Art. 5.7 governance with structured triggers for insufficiency, provisional-measure templates, evidence acquisition plans, periodic review SLAs, and audit-ready decision records supporting proportionality and WTO defensibility
questions.text: Where partnership outputs implicate sanitary/phytosanitary (SPS) measures, does the agent apply WTO SPS Agreement Article 5.7 by (1) identifying when scientific evidence is insufficient, (2) implementing provisional measures with documented rationale, (3) actively seeking additional information for a more objective risk assessment, and (4) reviewing/updating measures within a reasonable period with recorded decision trails?

patient-lifecycle.euAIActClassification: Art. 6(1) and Annex I (Regulation (EU) 2017/745 MDR, 2017/746 IVDR) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a medical device; Annex III §5(d) for emergency healthcare patient triage; §5(a) for public-authority eligibility decisions on healthcare services
keyRisks: Misdiagnosis from AI clinical decision support without adequate validation

Prognostic model bias leading to disparate care quality across demographics

questions.text: Does the agent enforce wastewater discharge standards per ZDHC Manufacturing Restricted Substances List (MRSL) v3.1 for wet processing facilities?

questions.l1: No labor condition assessment; supply chain labor practices are not monitored or verified by the agent
questions.l3: Agent integrates with social audit platforms (SMETA/SA8000) and flags facilities with non-conformances, but does not perform continuous monitoring or worker voice integration
questions.l5: Comprehensive labor rights monitoring with real-time worker voice channels, predictive risk scoring for forced labor indicators per ILO C029, child labor detection per C182, and transparent remediation tracking with verified corrective actions
questions.regulatoryRef: ILO Convention C029 Art. 2; ILO Convention C182 Art. 3
questions.text: Does the agent assess labor conditions in the supply chain per ILO Conventions C029 (Forced Labour) and C182 (Child Labour) through facility audit integration?

questions.l1: No environmental claim verification; sustainability marketing claims are generated without substantiation or lifecycle assessment backing
questions.l3: Agent calculates basic environmental metrics (carbon, water) using industry averages and flags unsubstantiated claims, but does not perform product-specific LCA per ISO 14044
questions.l5: Full lifecycle assessment integration per ISO 14044 with product-specific primary data, automated green claim substantiation per EU Green Claims Directive, third-party verification readiness, and transparent methodology disclosure
questions.text: Does the agent calculate and verify environmental impact claims per EU Green Claims Directive proposal Article 3 substantiation requirements?

questions.l1: No EPR tracking; end-of-life obligations for textile products are not managed or reported
questions.l3: Agent tracks EPR registration and fee obligations across jurisdictions, but does not optimize product design for recyclability or manage take-back logistics
questions.l5: Autonomous EPR lifecycle management with design-for-recyclability optimization, automated fee calculation across all EU member state schemes, take-back logistics coordination, and material recovery rate tracking against targets
questions.text: Does the agent manage Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) obligations per EU Waste Framework Directive 2008/98/EC Article 8a for textile products?

questions.l1: No recycled content verification; claims about recycled material percentages are unsubstantiated
questions.l3: Agent tracks recycled content certificates and transaction certificates per GRS, but chain of custody gaps exist at material blending and conversion stages
questions.l5: End-to-end chain of custody with mass balance verification at every conversion point, automated transaction certificate reconciliation, recycled content percentage validation with cryptographic proof, and audit-ready documentation per GRS 4.0
questions.text: Does the agent maintain chain of custody documentation per Global Recycled Standard (GRS) 4.0 Section 3 for recycled content claims?

questions.l1: No finished product safety testing integration; consumer-facing textiles are not verified against harmful substance limits
questions.l3: Agent validates test reports against OEKO-TEX Standard 100 product class limits, but does not proactively manage testing schedules or track certification renewal
questions.l5: Proactive consumer safety management with automated testing schedule coordination, real-time limit value verification against OEKO-TEX Appendix 4 by product class, certification lifecycle management, and consumer transparency through scannable safety verification
questions.text: Does the agent verify consumer product safety per OEKO-TEX Standard 100 Appendix 4 limit values for harmful substances in finished textiles?

questions.l1: No CS3D or forced labour compliance; AI supply chain agents do not perform mandatory human rights due diligence or screen for forced labour indicators in textile sourcing
questions.l3: Agent implements basic supply chain risk screening and flags high-risk suppliers, but does not automate CS3D Art. 10 adverse impact identification or EU Forced Labour Regulation Art. 3 product-level investigation triggers
questions.l5: Full CS3D compliance with Art. 10 adverse impact identification and mitigation, EU Forced Labour Regulation Art. 3 investigation automation, product-level forced labour risk assessment, supply chain remediation tracking, and competent authority notification capability per Art. 4
questions.regulatoryRef: EU CS3D 2024/1760 Art. 10; EU Forced Labour Reg 2024/3015 Art. 3
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive 2024/1760 Article 10 supply chain AI obligations and EU Forced Labour Regulation 2024/3015 import-ban enforcement for textile supply chains?

questions.l1: No minimum-age controls; audits do not explicitly check C138 thresholds or hazardous-work restrictions; remediation is ad-hoc
questions.l3: Agent checks minimum-age records in social audits and flags noncompliance, but coverage is limited to tier-1/2 and remediation tracking is incomplete
questions.l5: Continuous minimum-age assurance across tiers with worker-age verification safeguards, hazardous-task controls for young workers, grievance channels, verified remediation closure, and audit-ready evidence trails aligned to C138
questions.text: Does the agent verify minimum-age compliance and hazardous-work protections per ILO Convention C138 (Minimum Age) Articles 2–3 across all textile supply chain tiers, including remediation and monitoring of young-worker conditions?

questions.l1: No OECD DDG implementation; supplier risk processes are informal and not aligned to §III expectations
questions.l3: Agent performs supplier mapping and basic risk screening, but does not fully operationalize §III (stakeholder engagement, grievance, mitigation effectiveness tracking)
questions.l5: Full OECD DDG §III operationalization with end-to-end supplier mapping, structured risk taxonomy, time-bound mitigation and leverage plans, worker/stakeholder engagement loops, grievance intake-to-closure workflow, and effectiveness measurement with auditable evidence
questions.text: Does the agent implement risk-based due diligence for garment & footwear supply chains per OECD Due Diligence Guidance (Garment & Footwear) §III, including supplier mapping, risk identification, mitigation plans, stakeholder engagement, and grievance/complaints mechanisms?

questions.l1: No SVHC-criteria mapping; only ad-hoc checks against lists without criteria traceability
questions.l3: Agent screens against the SVHC candidate list, but cannot explain Art.57 category rationale or prioritize substitution beyond list membership
questions.l5: Art.57-aware SVHC governance: criteria-based classification, continuous candidate-list monitoring, substitution planning, concentration/threshold tracking, and auditable rationale for chemical decisions across tiers
questions.text: Does the agent operationalize REACH SVHC identification criteria per REACH (EC) 1907/2006 Article 57 (CMR, PBT/vPvB, endocrine disruptors, equivalent concern) and map them to candidate-list screening and substitution decisions for textile chemistries?

questions.l1: No 2024/1781 alignment; DPP data is incomplete and not mapped to ecodesign delegated-act requirements
questions.l3: Agent produces a basic DPP, but does not map required attributes to Art.5 delegated acts or ensure ongoing lifecycle updates
questions.l5: Delegated-act-ready DPP: mandatory attributes mapping, interoperable data carrier, signed data integrity, lifecycle updates (repair/reuse/recycling), and compliance evidence generation aligned to Arts.5/8
questions.text: Does the agent ensure Digital Product Passport (DPP) implementation under Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Article 8 is complete, and that DPP data attributes and lifecycle updates satisfy ecodesign requirements and delegated acts issued under Article 5 for textiles?

questions.l1: No article-level SVHC tracking; recipients and consumers receive no Article 33 information
questions.l3: Agent flags SVHC content above 0.1% w/w from supplier declarations, but recipient notices and consumer replies are manual and not tracked against the 45-day limit
questions.l5: Article-level SVHC concentration records updated on each Candidate List revision, automatic Article 33(1) notices to recipients, and consumer requests answered and evidenced within 45 days
questions.text: For every textile article containing a REACH Candidate List substance above 0.1% w/w, does the agent generate the supplier-to-recipient safety information required by REACH Article 33(1) and answer consumer requests under Article 33(2) within 45 days?

questions.l1: Disposal of unsold stock is not tracked; destruction decisions are not checked against Article 25
questions.l3: Agent tracks unsold stock and discards, but derogations are not evidenced and the Article 24 disclosure is compiled by hand
questions.l5: Disposal workflow refuses prohibited destruction, requires an evidenced derogation for each exception, routes stock to reuse or recycling, and publishes the Article 24 figures (quantities, reasons, destinations) from the system of record
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Ecodesign Regulation 2024/1781 Arts. 24-25, Annex VII
questions.text: Does the agent block the destruction of unsold apparel, clothing accessories and footwear prohibited by Ecodesign Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Article 25 and Annex VII, record any derogation relied on, and produce the Article 24 disclosure of unsold consumer products discarded?
